job.title: Dock hand
job.description:

Are you an experienced Dock Hand looking for your next opportunity with a leading national freight and logistics operation? We are currently seeking reliable, safety-focused and hardworking individuals to join a busy transport and distribution team based in Upper Coomera.
This is a fast-paced role suited to candidates who enjoy physical work, can work efficiently in a team environment, and are committed to maintaining high safety standards.

What's on Offer?
  • Competitive pay rates of $38.61
  • Ongoing casual opportunities with potential for long-term work
  • Immediate starts available
  • Supportive team environment
  • Day and Afternoon shifts available
Available Shift Times
  • 10:00am - 6:30pm (30-minute unpaid break)
  • 1:30pm - 10:00pm (30-minute unpaid break)

  • Loading and unloading freight from trailers and dock areas
  • Sorting and staging freight for dispatch
  • Manual handling of parcels and general freight

  • Physically fit and capable of repetitive manual handling

About You You are a motivated and dependable team player who takes pride in working safely and efficiently. You thrive in busy warehouse environments and are willing to contribute wherever required to ensure freight is processed accurately and on time.
If you're looking for a rewarding opportunity, click APPLY NOW and submit your application today.

job.title: Engineering Specialists – Multiple Disciplines | APS 6, EL1 & EL2
job.description:
Chandler Macleod is recruiting on behalf of our client for exceptional opportunities within a high-profile Federal Government agency supporting one of Australia’s most significant long-term defence capability programs.

We are seeking experienced Engineers from a wide range of disciplines, at APS 6, Executive Level 1 and Executive Level 2, to contribute to a major naval defence capability program that will shape Australia’s security, workforce, industrial capability and supply chains for decades to come.

About the Role
This major naval defence capability program is a historic and transformative endeavour for Australia. This whole-of-nation effort brings together government, industry and international partners to deliver one of the most complex engineering programs in the nation’s history.

Engineers will work across technical governance, assurance, certification, design review and through-life support of advanced naval platforms and systems. Roles range from highly specialist to broad, depending on your discipline and experience, and you may have the opportunity to work across streams. Successful candidates may also have the opportunity to nominate for international placements with overseas partner organisations, with in-country training and support provided beforehand.

These positions attract a competitive remuneration package, including an additional premium for critical capability disciplines and generous superannuation.

About the Team
You’ll join engineering branches responsible for the technical governance, safety certification and objective quality evidence (OQE) that underpin the safe, effective and sovereign operation of Australia’s future naval capability. Teams combine civilian and military personnel from diverse disciplines, and the culture puts people, technical development, integrity and safety first.

Engineering Disciplines
We are interested in hearing from Engineers with experience in one or more of the following:

  • Mechanical, structural and materials engineering (including FEA and structural/materials modelling)
  • Electrical, electronic and mechatronic engineering
  • Instrumentation and control
  • Systems engineering and systems integration
  • Power, propulsion and energy systems
  • Safety case development, system safety and environmental protection
  • Marine structures, naval architecture, weld design and shock/survivability
  • Signature management (acoustic and non-acoustic), trials, measurement and analysis
  • Modelling and simulation (structural, thermal-hydraulics, fluid-structure interaction)
  • Field support, engineering investigations, and decommissioning and disposal
Key Responsibilities
Depending on level and discipline, responsibilities may include:

  • Reviewing, evaluating and recommending courses of action on designs, specifications and deviations to support approval and certification decisions
  • Developing the methodologies, processes and OQE used to assure and certify engineering systems
  • Contributing to safety cases, regulatory submissions, and plans, processes and procedures
  • Working with national and international partners, industry, regulators and academia to apply engineering best practice
  • Participating in international meetings and workshops, sometimes outside standard Australian working hours
  • Preparing high-quality briefs, reports and presentations to inform senior decision-makers
  • At EL1 and EL2, leading teams, planning and managing technical programs and resources, and mentoring developing engineers
About You
You will demonstrate:

  • A Bachelor of Engineering (or equivalent) that satisfies the Washington Accord for recognition as a Professional Engineer
  • Strong technical competence in your discipline and a willingness to keep learning alongside leading experts in novel technologies
  • Sound judgement and a systems-thinking approach to identifying and managing risk
  • Well-developed written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain complex technical concepts to a range of audiences
  • The ability to build effective relationships across government, industry and international stakeholders
  • For EL1 and EL2 roles, demonstrated leadership, supervision and mentoring experience
Highly regarded but not essential:

  • Chartered Professional Engineer (Engineers Australia), Registered Professional Engineer (Professionals Australia), or membership of an equivalent institution such as RINA, IMechE, IMarEST or IEEE (or the ability to obtain it within 12 months)
  • Experience in Defence, defence industry, maritime, energy or other highly regulated, safety-critical sectors
  • Experience working with overseas partners or within multi-regulator environments
  • Openness to an international placement of 2 to 3 years
You don’t need Defence experience. Engineers from all applicable industries are encouraged to apply.

Locations: Adelaide / Port Adelaide – SA, Canberra – ACT, Melbourne – VIC, Perth – WA, Sydney – NSW
 

Security Requirement
Applicants must be Australian citizens and able to obtain and maintain a minimum Negative Vetting Level 1 (NV1) security clearance. Some roles may require a higher clearance level.

Apply Now
If you are an experienced Engineer looking to apply your expertise to a once-in-a-generation national program, we encourage you to apply today. Please submit your current resume. Shortlisted candidates may be asked for a short statement (up to 600 words) on how their skills, knowledge and experience fit their chosen discipline.

At Chandler Macleod, we are committed to fostering a diverse workforce where everyone is welcome. We encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, women, neurodiverse individuals, people living with a disability, and the LGBTIQA+ community. You can read more about our commitment to diversity and inclusion at: https://www.chandlermacleod.com/diversity-and-inclusion.

job.title: LO Forklift - Horsley Park
job.description:
LO Operators - Amazon Horsley Park. 

Looking for your next opportunity with Amazon Australia? Chandler Macleod is recruiting LO Operators to join the team at Amazon’s Fulfilment Centre in Horsley Park.

What’s on offer:
  • Work at Amazon Australia’s Horsley Park Fulfilment Centre
  • Training and ongoing support provided
  • Day shift opportunities
  • 10-hour shifts
  • Employee parking available onsite
  • Flexible casual work
Roles will commence from Wednesday 4th November 2026

Experience isn't necessary - we will train you. You must have a valid LO FL license.

Day shifts rates start from $38.76. Night shift and Weekend incur penalties 

About the role:
This is a casual opportunity requiring availability across 4 days per week, including 1 weekend day.

Your shifts will include a combination of LO forklift operation and general warehouse duties. Once onboarded and trained, you will be required to successfully complete a competency assessment before operating independently.

Attention to detail, accuracy, safety and the ability to follow standard processes are essential.

Key responsibilities:

  • Operating an LO forklift once trained and assessed as competent
  • Loading and unloading trucks
  • Packing and unpacking boxes
  • Receiving and storing stock
  • Picking items using an RF scanner, with training provided
  • Organising and distributing customer orders
  • Maintaining a clean and organised warehouse
  • Following safety, quality and production standards
  • Standing and walking for extended periods
  • Lifting and moving products weighing up to 23kg

What we’re looking for:
  • Availability across 4 days per week, including 1 weekend day
  • Strong commitment to safety and quality
  • Good attention to detail and ability to follow processes
  • Ability to undertake the physical requirements of the role
  • Right to work in Australia
Successful applicants will be employed by Chandler Macleod on a temporary assignment with Amazon and will be required to complete relevant background and police checks, as well as drug and alcohol testing.

Ready to take the next step?

job.title: Senior Recruitment Consultant
job.description:
Senior Recruitment Consultant
Own the relationship | Drive the growth | Deliver the outcomes!

Chandler Macleod is seeking an experienced Senior Recruitment Consultant to lead and grow a portfolio of key mining customers across Queensland.
This is a highly visible role responsible for managing strategic customer relationships, driving commercial growth, ensuring workforce delivery excellence, and acting as the primary point of accountability for customer outcomes.

Working closely with Recruitment, Operations, Safety, Payroll, and Support Teams, you will partner with customers to deliver workforce solutions that meet operational demands while creating long-term value for both the customer and Chandler Macleod.

The Role
  • Own and manage key customer relationships across the Queensland mining portfolio.
  • Build trusted partnerships with operational, commercial, and leadership stakeholders.
  • Identify and secure opportunities to grow workforce demand and expand service offerings.
  • Drive job order generation, workforce growth, and account development initiatives.
  • Partner with recruitment teams to ensure workforce requirements are fulfilled efficiently and effectively.
  • Lead workforce planning discussions and provide proactive workforce solutions.
  • Act as the escalation point for customer and workforce-related matters.
  • Support employee and industrial relations matters, investigations, performance management, and workforce issues.
  • Oversee safety, incident, injury management, and return-to-work processes in partnership with internal stakeholders.
  • Provide leadership and support to onsite Workforce Coordinators.
  • Ensure contractual obligations, compliance requirements, and service standards are consistently achieved.

About You

To be successful in this role, you will bring:
  • Demonstrated experience in Account Management, Workforce Solutions, Recruitment, Labour Hire, or a related industry.
  • A proven track record of growing customer accounts and delivering commercial outcomes.
  • Strong stakeholder management and relationship-building capability.
  • Experience working within mining, resources, industrial, or operational environments.
  • Knowledge of workforce planning, recruitment, mobilisation, and workforce management.
  • Experience managing employee relations, industrial relations, investigations, and workplace issues.
  • Sound understanding of workplace health and safety, incident management, injury management, and return-to-work processes.
  • Strong commercial acumen and business development capability.
  • Excellent communication, negotiation, and influencing skills.
  • The ability to operate autonomously, solve problems, and manage competing priorities.

Career Development Opportunity
  • Expand your experience across account management, workforce solutions, and business development.
  • Broaden your exposure to commercial management and strategic customer engagement.
  • Develop leadership capability through mentoring and supporting onsite teams.
  • Build the skills and experience required for future leadership roles within Chandler Macleod.

If you're a relationship-focused account leader who thrives on customer engagement, business growth, and delivering workforce solutions in a fast-paced mining environment, we'd love to hear from you.

At Chandler Macleod, we are committed to fostering a diverse workforce where everyone is welcome.
We encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, women, neurodiverse individuals, people living with disability, and members of the LGBTIQA+ community.
You can read more about our commitment to diversity and inclusion at: https://www.chandlermacleod.com/diversity-and-inclusion

job.title: Civil Marine Maintenance Supervisor
job.description:
Position: Civil Marine Maintenance Supervisor
Contract Duration: 12 months duration
Location: Fremantle, WA
Hours per week: Monday to Friday - 40 hours per week
Salary: $79.46 per hour (flat rate on all hours)

About the Role
The Marine Civil Maintenance Supervisor is responsible for planned and reactive maintenance works across the Fremantle Ports Inner Harbour berth, jetties and seawall breakwaters, including scoping, cost and schedule management, safety and quality control, and on-site supervision of contractors.

In doing so, the position ensures contractor compliance with designs, specifications and industry best practice, and executes day-to-day maintenance of marine civil assets including piles, suspended deck, superstructure and seawalls.

Key Duties
  • Responsible for preparing scopes of work for reactive and planned maintenance, reviewing inspection reports and the asset register, and assessing maintenance requirements and safety issues
  • Responsible for on-site supervision of contractors as surveillance officer, monitoring compliance with Quality and Safety Management Plans and statutory requirements
  • Facilitate and coordinate site and safety inductions and permits for contractors’ staff, and manage the safety, quality and delivery performance of contractors
  • Assist the Superintendent with preparation of maintenance project budgets and work schedules and update the asset register with completed works and condition changes
  • Coordinate document control, material procurement, warehousing and testing to ensure compliance with specifications and schedules
  • Liaise with contractors, customers and other managers and supervisors (e.g. Marine Services, Port Operations, Safety and Environment, External Affairs) whose areas of work are affected by the team’s output
  • Liaise with the Marine Civil Infrastructure Superintendent to prepare tender documents, evaluate tenders and make recommendations for awarding project works
  • Responsible for ensuring Fremantle Ports Quality, Safety and Environmental standards, guidelines and procedures are achieved and adhered to within their area of influence

Qualifications & Experience
Essential:
  • Trade qualifications in Civil and Marine Construction, or extensive relevant experience (7+ years)
  • Tertiary qualifications in Civil, Construction or a related engineering discipline, and/or qualifications in Contract Administration, Project Management or Maintenance Management
Desirable:
  • Experience in the construction, inspection, maintenance and repair of seawalls, breakwaters and other coastal marine structures, with maintenance supervision and contract administration skills
  • Sound knowledge of statutory legislation and OH&S regulations relating to maintenance management, with demonstrated ability to implement and ensure a safe work environment
  • Good written, verbal and negotiation skills, and possession of a current ‘C’ or ‘CA’ class driver’s licence

job.title: Dozer Operators
job.description:
Dozer Operator

• 8:6 / 7:7 roster | FIFO from Perth
• Opportunity working at Rio Tinto at Brockman 4

Rio Tinto is a global mining and materials company operating in 35 countries, producing the materials essential to modern life. Their operations are built on safety, innovation, inclusion and creating value for communities, customers and shareholders.

job.title: S26 Project Manager - NPI
job.description:
Chandler Macleod is partnering with a well-established WA-based contractor delivering Non-Process Infrastructure (NPI) works across remote resources and energy projects. With a strong pipeline of camp / modular village installs, expansions and supporting infrastructure, we’re looking for an experienced Project Manager with Section 26 to take projects from early mobilisation through to execution on site.

This is a permanent opportunity with an immediate start available for the right person.

The Opportunity You’ll initially spend time based in Perth supporting pre-mobilisation and planning, then transition to site on a standard 2:1 roster to lead delivery.

Projects are typically in the $8M–$10M range and include accommodation villages, camp expansions and other NPI construction scopes across WA (and broader remote work as required).

Key Responsibilities
  • End-to-end project delivery (planning, mobilisation, execution, close-out)
  • Provide statutory supervision in line with WA WHS (Mines) obligations as required
  • Lead site teams and subcontractors to achieve safety, schedule, quality and cost outcomes
  • Drive a strong safety culture (pre-starts, JHAs/SWMS, permits, incident follow-up)
  • Client and stakeholder engagement, reporting and progress updates
  • Manage resourcing, productivity and performance across multiple work fronts
What We’re Looking For
  • Proven Project Management experience delivering NPI / construction projects in remote environments
  • Section 26 (S26) Statutory Supervisor (preferred)
  • Strong preference for candidates with tier-one contractor-side delivery experience (camp/modular is highly regarded)
  • Ability to work Perth-based pre-mob, then commit to 2:1 site roster
  • Solid understanding of remote construction execution, subcontractor management and site systems
What’s On Offer
  • Permanent role with long-term project pipeline
  • 2:1 roster once mobilised
  • Exposure to a strong portfolio of NPI/camp infrastructure works across major resource clients
  • Competitive remuneration package (discussed with shortlisted candidates)
Apply If this aligns with your background, send through your CV and we’ll arrange a confidential discussion.

At Chandler Macleod, we are committed to fostering a diverse workforce where everyone is welcome. We encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, women, neurodiverse, people living with a disability and the LGBTIQA+ community.

You can read more about our commitment to diversity and inclusion at https://www.chandlermacleod.com/diversity-and-inclusion.

job.title: Assistant Production Manager
job.description:
Assistant Production Manager – Permanent | Hindmarsh, SA
$95k–$107k + super + 10% KPI bonus | 06:00–14:45 | On-site

This is a true 2IC production leadership role with real scope (~50 headcount) and a clear succession / progression pathway. You’ll be visible on the floor, driving safety, delivery and continuous improvement in a stable operation with ongoing investment.

About the role
We’re seeking an Assistant Production Manager to support the Production Manager in running day-to-day production operations, driving efficiency, quality, and on-time delivery. This is a hands-on, floor-based leadership role where you’ll work closely with supervisors and cross-functional leaders to deliver strong customer outcomes while maintaining safety, compliance, and continuous improvement standards.

Who this suits
This role is best suited to a current Assistant Production Manager (or equivalent 2IC in production) with proven experience leading teams in a manufacturing/production environment (FMCG highly regarded). You’re an extroverted, relationship-first leader with high energy and a growth mindset—comfortable building trust on the floor and lifting standards through others.


Please note: this position is not designed as a first-time leadership step-up; we’re looking for someone already operating at Assistant Production Manager / 2IC level.

Team & environment
  • Leadership scope of ~50 reports (direct/indirect) including 5 team leaders
  • Some overtime may be required during peak periods 
Key responsibilities
  • Plan and schedule daily production to achieve on-time, in-full delivery and quality standards
  • Coordinate labour planning, rostering/scheduling, and labour forecasting to match production needs
  • Monitor performance data and coach teams to achieve daily efficiency and quality targets
  • Support and lead Lean/CI ways of working and continuous improvement on the floor (including 5S)
  • Apply and maintain HACCP principles, ensuring non-conformances are controlled and corrective actions are completed
  • Partner with Service/Customer teams to ensure customer feedback is actioned promptly and service excellence targets are met
  • Assist with recruitment, onboarding, training, and performance management for production staff (including engagement with agencies as required)
  • Work with Engineering to align equipment uptime, maintenance schedules, and production requirements
  • Ensure compliance with WHS policies, procedures, and reporting requirements (including payroll-related timelines where relevant)

About you (must-haves)
  • Proven capability in rostering/scheduling and labour forecasting within production/manufacturing
  • Strong people leadership: coaching, performance management, and leading team leaders
  • Sound understanding of production operations and service/quality delivery
  • Exposure to budgeting / labour cost control
  • Confident engaging with recruitment partners/agencies to meet workforce demand
  • Strong commitment to safety and legal/WHS compliance
  • Intermediate Microsoft Office skills (Excel desirable)
  • Current driver’s licence

Highly regarded
  • Lean / Continuous Improvement tools including 5S
  • Systems exposure: SAP / XCM
  • Experience with Spindle (laundry operations / workforce software)

What’s on offer
  • $95k–$107k + super + 10% KPI bonus
  • Permanent full-time role with a stable employer and strong job security
  • Internal progression culture, succession planning intent, and tailored development programs
  • Facility upgrades/investment and a supportive team environment focused on safety, quality, and continuous improvement
  • Early shift pattern supporting work/life balance

Pre-employment checks may include reference checks and other role-relevant compliance requirements.

job.title: Airline Chef
job.description:
Airline Production Chef
$83000–$88,000 pa (Pro Rata)
Perth Airport

Are you an experienced Chef with a passion for authentic flavours and high‑volume production? Join an airline catering team and play a key role in creating exceptional in‑flight meals enjoyed by passengers across the world.

Chandler Macleod is seeking Production Chefs who can bring expertise and consistency to our large‑scale client's airline food production operations.

About the Role
As an Airline Production Chef, you will prepare high‑quality dishes across a variety of Asian and Western cuisines — tailored for airline passengers in both Economy and Premium cabins. Working in a fast‑paced production kitchen, you’ll ensure every dish meets strict taste, presentation, and food‑safety standards.

This is initially a casual position (full-time hours) with annualised earnings ranging between $82K - $88K p/a. Permanent employment opportunities are considered following the successful completion of the first six months.  

Key Responsibilities
  • Prepare and cook authentic dishes in a bulk cooking production environment
  • Ensure consistency in taste, quality, portioning, and presentation
  • Maintain strict food‑safety compliance (HACCP and Airline Protocols)

job.title: Business Change Analyst and Transformation - Policy, Programs and Engagement
job.description:
About the company:

The Agency is a national government organisation responsible for delivering major digital transformation initiatives that improve the way services are accessed and delivered across Australia. Working closely with government, industry, healthcare providers, and consumers, the Agency leads programs that drive innovation, improve service delivery, and support better outcomes for Australians.
The Agency offers a collaborative and inclusive work environment where employees are encouraged to contribute ideas, build strong stakeholder relationships, and deliver meaningful outcomes through large-scale national reforms.

About the Team

The National Program Delivery team is responsible for implementing a diverse portfolio of nationally significant programs and projects. The team works across multiple stakeholders to support the successful delivery of digital initiatives, business improvements, and reform activities.
The team operates in a highly collaborative environment, partnering with business areas, government stakeholders, delivery partners, and industry representatives to ensure change is effectively managed and implemented.

About the Role
The Change Analyst supports the successful delivery of large-scale digital transformation programs and projects. Reporting within a fast-paced and collaborative environment, the role focuses on helping stakeholders understand, prepare for, and adopt new systems, processes, and ways of working.
Working closely with project teams, business areas, and external stakeholders, the Change Analyst provides analysis, coordination, and support across a range of change management activities to ensure successful implementation and adoption of key initiatives.
This is an excellent opportunity for a candidate who enjoys stakeholder engagement, problem-solving, data analysis, and supporting organisational change.
.
Key Responsibilities
  • Conduct change impact assessments to understand how initiatives affect stakeholders, business processes, and service delivery.
  • Identify and analyse stakeholder groups, their needs, and potential barriers to adoption.
  • Support the planning and delivery of change management activities across multiple projects and programs.
  • Coordinate stakeholder engagement and communication activities.
  • Gather and analyse feedback, data, and insights to support decision-making and implementation planning.
  • Monitor stakeholder readiness and adoption outcomes.
  • Track and report on project progress, risks, issues, and change activities.
  • Identify and escalate implementation risks and barriers to adoption.
  • Prepare reports, briefings, presentations, and stakeholder communications.
  • Work closely with project teams and stakeholders to support successful implementation and transition activities.
You Must Have
 
  • Experience within government, healthcare, or large-scale transformation environments.
  • Qualifications or certifications in Change Management, Project Management, Business Analysis, Agile, PRINCE2, Prosci, PMP, Scrum, or related disciplines.
  • Experience supporting technology or system implementation projects.
  • Understanding of change management methodologies, stakeholder readiness, and adoption principles.
  • Experience supporting change management, project delivery, business improvement, or digital transformation initiatives.
  • Strong stakeholder engagement and relationship management skills.
  • Experience analysing data, stakeholder feedback, and business information to support decision-making.
  • Ability to identify risks, issues, and implementation challenges and contribute to practical solutions.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Experience preparing reports, presentations, briefing papers, and stakeholder communications.
  • Strong organisational and coordination skills with the ability to manage competing priorities.
  • Ability to build effective working relationships with internal and external stakeholders.
  • Strong attention to detail and problem-solving capability.
  • Baseline Security Clearance Required

Benefits:
  • ASAP start (pending Federal Police Clearance)
  • 12-month assignment with possibility of extension
  • Location:  Brisbane, Canberra, Sydney



How to apply:

Chandler Macleod is an equal opportunity employer as part of our commitment to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people, disability and culturally and linguistics candidates are also encouraged to apply.

Please note the successful candidate for the role must hold Australian Citizenship.

Application closes on the  3 November 2026

job.description:

  • Provide high-level executive support to three General Managers, ensuring seamless management of day-to-day operations.
  • Manage complex and constantly changing diaries, prioritising appointments and resolving scheduling conflicts.
  • Coordinate domestic travel arrangements, meeting logistics, agendas, presentations, and associated documentation.

  • Support leadership teams with project coordination and administrative initiatives as required.
  • Act as a keyy point of contact for all stakeholders whilst maintaining strong working relationships

Essential Experience

  • Strong organisational and time-management skills with the ability to balance competing priorities.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Experience preparing professional reports, presentations, and correspondence.

job.title: Director Infrastructure Operations
job.description:
Chandler Macleod is recruiting on behalf of our client for an exceptional opportunity within a high-profile Federal Government agency supporting Australia’s most significant long-term capability program.

This is a unique chance for an experienced EL2 Director Infrastructure Operations to join the Australian Submarine Agency (ASA), contributing to a nationally significant defence initiative that will shape Australia’s security, workforce, industrial capability and supply chains for decades to come.

About the Role
Working within the Australian Submarine Agency environment, the EL2 Director Infrastructure Operations will lead a critical function within the Infrastructure Planning, Performance and Integration (IPPI) team, supporting the delivery of a complex, nationally significant infrastructure portfolio.

The acquisition of conventionally-armed, nuclear-powered submarines is an historic and transformative endeavour for Australia. This whole-of-nation effort will transform Australia’s economic and national security landscape for decades to come.
The ASA’s Infrastructure Planning and Coordination (IP&C) Division is responsible for planning and coordinating the delivery of physical infrastructure that will:
  • Enable AUKUS partners to have a rotational presence at HMAS Stirling
  • Support Australia’s acquisition and sustainment of Virginia Class submarines
  • Deliver Australia’s sovereign build and sustainment of SSN-AUKUS submarines
In this role, you will use commercial, workforce, financial and business operations levers to improve organisational performance, strengthen delivery confidence and enable informed executive decision-making.
This position is eligible for an additional remuneration benefit known within ASA as a Building Capability Payment (BCP), applied in addition to base salary for critical capability disciplines.

About the Team
The Infrastructure Planning and Coordination (IP&C) Division coordinates the infrastructure that enables Australia’s nuclear-powered submarine capability. The work spans major programs and sites across Western Australia and South Australia, bringing together government, industry and international partners to deliver nationally significant outcomes.
You’ll join a collaborative, high-performing environment where you can shape strategy, influence delivery outcomes and contribute to one of Australia’s most complex infrastructure portfolios.

Key Responsibilities: 
You will be responsible for leading and enabling infrastructure operations outcomes, including:
  • Leading and growing high-performing teams, building capability and fostering a culture of accountability and collaboration
  • Driving continuous improvement across reporting, governance, information management and organisational performance
  • Providing strategic leadership and sound judgement to solve complex problems and balance competing priorities
  • Strengthening delivery confidence through robust performance oversight, insights and operational levers
  • Applying strong commercial, financial and business management acumen to translate data into decisions and action
  • Influencing outcomes across diverse stakeholder groups where success relies on collaboration rather than direct authority
  • Identifying and managing enterprise risks, opportunities and dependencies to improve delivery outcomes
  • Operating effectively in ambiguity, providing clear advice and direction in evolving environments
  • Preparing and delivering high-quality advice and communication to senior executives, government stakeholders and delivery partners
About You:
You will demonstrate:
  • Proven leadership experience in complex operational, portfolio, program or infrastructure environments
  • Strong commercial, financial and business management capability
  • Experience improving organisational performance through governance, reporting and insight-led decision-making
  • Demonstrated ability to influence outcomes across multiple stakeholders and competing priorities
  • High-level written and verbal communication skills, with experience advising senior leaders
Security Requirement
Applicants must be able to obtain and maintain a Negative Vetting Level 2 (NV2) security clearance.

Apply Now

If you are an experienced senior leader looking to contribute to a once-in-a-generation national program, we encourage you to apply today.

At Chandler Macleod, we are committed to fostering a diverse workforce where everyone is welcome. We encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, women, neurodiverse individuals, people living with a disability, and the LGBTIQA+ community. job.title: Senior Electrical Engineer
job.description:
Senior / Principal Electrical Engineer

Location: Adelaide, SA
Contract: 12 Months | ASAP Start
Industry: Mining, Metals & Minerals

About the Role
An opportunity exists for an experienced Senior Electrical Engineer or Principal Electrical Engineer to join a well-established engineering team supporting multiple mining, metals and mineral processing projects.

This role is ideally suited to an engineer with strong brownfield project experience, particularly within copper, base metals, mineral processing, heavy industry or resources environments. You'll be involved across the full project lifecycle, from early scoping and concept development through to detailed design, construction support and commissioning.
Working within a multidisciplinary team, you'll provide practical, fit-for-purpose engineering solutions while managing stakeholder relationships and delivering multiple projects concurrently.

Key Responsibilities
  • Deliver electrical engineering solutions across concept, design, execution and commissioning phases.
  • Prepare and review engineering calculations, drawings, specifications and technical documentation.
  • Develop fit-for-purpose electrical designs considering safety, operability, maintainability and lifecycle requirements.
  • Lead or support project scope development, estimates, schedules and resource planning.
  • Participate in HAZIDs, HAZOPs, Safety-in-Design and design reviews.
  • Support site inspections, field engineering, construction and commissioning activities.
  • Coordinate with clients, contractors, project managers and multidisciplinary engineering teams.
  • Manage multiple projects while ensuring delivery to schedule, budget and quality requirements.
  • Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives and digital engineering practices.
Principal Engineer Responsibilities
Candidates operating at Principal level will also:
  • Provide technical leadership and mentoring.
  • Lead discipline deliverables and project resources.
  • Act as the primary client interface for electrical engineering matters.
  • Manage technical risk, design reviews and engineering quality.
  • Coordinate discipline activities across multiple projects and teams.
About You
You will have:
  • Bachelor of Electrical Engineering (or equivalent).
  • Minimum 10 years' experience within mining, minerals, metals, energy or heavy industrial sectors.
  • Strong brownfield project experience.
  • Proven ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously.
  • Experience delivering projects from concept through to execution.
  • Strong client engagement and stakeholder management skills.
  • Excellent understanding of Australian electrical standards.
Technical Experience
Experience in some or all of the following is highly regarded:
  • HV/LV power distribution systems
  • HV switchgear and MCC design
  • Equipment sizing and cable routing
  • Earthing and lighting design
  • Arc flash assessments
  • Protection systems and relay settings
  • Instrumentation and control interfaces
  • Electrical calculations and design verification
  • SLDs, schematics, layouts and cable schedules
  • FATs, SATs and commissioning support
  • Technical specifications, datasheets, ITPs and MTOs
  • Shutdown planning and brownfield modifications
  • Cost estimating and project execution planning
Requirements
  • Unrestricted Australian working rights.
  • Ability to work from the office.
  • Available to commence ASAP.
Apply Now
If you're an experienced Senior or Principal Electrical Engineer with a background in mining, minerals, metals or heavy industrial projects, we'd like to hear from you.

job.title: Engineering Specialists – Multiple Disciplines | APS 6, EL1 & EL2
job.description:
Chandler Macleod is recruiting on behalf of our client for exceptional opportunities within a high-profile Federal Government agency supporting one of Australia’s most significant long-term defence capability programs.

We are seeking experienced Engineers from a wide range of disciplines, at APS 6, Executive Level 1 and Executive Level 2, to contribute to a major naval defence capability program that will shape Australia’s security, workforce, industrial capability and supply chains for decades to come.

About the Role
This major naval defence capability program is a historic and transformative endeavour for Australia. This whole-of-nation effort brings together government, industry and international partners to deliver one of the most complex engineering programs in the nation’s history.

Engineers will work across technical governance, assurance, certification, design review and through-life support of advanced naval platforms and systems. Roles range from highly specialist to broad, depending on your discipline and experience, and you may have the opportunity to work across streams. Successful candidates may also have the opportunity to nominate for international placements with overseas partner organisations, with in-country training and support provided beforehand.

These positions attract a competitive remuneration package, including an additional premium for critical capability disciplines and generous superannuation.

About the Team
You’ll join engineering branches responsible for the technical governance, safety certification and objective quality evidence (OQE) that underpin the safe, effective and sovereign operation of Australia’s future naval capability. Teams combine civilian and military personnel from diverse disciplines, and the culture puts people, technical development, integrity and safety first.

Engineering Disciplines
We are interested in hearing from Engineers with experience in one or more of the following:

  • Mechanical, structural and materials engineering (including FEA and structural/materials modelling)
  • Electrical, electronic and mechatronic engineering
  • Instrumentation and control
  • Systems engineering and systems integration
  • Power, propulsion and energy systems
  • Safety case development, system safety and environmental protection
  • Marine structures, naval architecture, weld design and shock/survivability
  • Signature management (acoustic and non-acoustic), trials, measurement and analysis
  • Modelling and simulation (structural, thermal-hydraulics, fluid-structure interaction)
  • Field support, engineering investigations, and decommissioning and disposal
Key Responsibilities
Depending on level and discipline, responsibilities may include:

  • Reviewing, evaluating and recommending courses of action on designs, specifications and deviations to support approval and certification decisions
  • Developing the methodologies, processes and OQE used to assure and certify engineering systems
  • Contributing to safety cases, regulatory submissions, and plans, processes and procedures
  • Working with national and international partners, industry, regulators and academia to apply engineering best practice
  • Participating in international meetings and workshops, sometimes outside standard Australian working hours
  • Preparing high-quality briefs, reports and presentations to inform senior decision-makers
  • At EL1 and EL2, leading teams, planning and managing technical programs and resources, and mentoring developing engineers
About You
You will demonstrate:

  • A Bachelor of Engineering (or equivalent) that satisfies the Washington Accord for recognition as a Professional Engineer
  • Strong technical competence in your discipline and a willingness to keep learning alongside leading experts in novel technologies
  • Sound judgement and a systems-thinking approach to identifying and managing risk
  • Well-developed written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain complex technical concepts to a range of audiences
  • The ability to build effective relationships across government, industry and international stakeholders
  • For EL1 and EL2 roles, demonstrated leadership, supervision and mentoring experience
Highly regarded but not essential:

  • Chartered Professional Engineer (Engineers Australia), Registered Professional Engineer (Professionals Australia), or membership of an equivalent institution such as RINA, IMechE, IMarEST or IEEE (or the ability to obtain it within 12 months)
  • Experience in Defence, defence industry, maritime, energy or other highly regulated, safety-critical sectors
  • Experience working with overseas partners or within multi-regulator environments
  • Openness to an international placement of 2 to 3 years
You don’t need Defence experience. Engineers from all applicable industries are encouraged to apply.

Locations: Adelaide / Port Adelaide – SA, Canberra – ACT, Melbourne – VIC, Perth – WA, Sydney – NSW
 

Security Requirement
Applicants must be Australian citizens and able to obtain and maintain a minimum Negative Vetting Level 1 (NV1) security clearance. Some roles may require a higher clearance level.

Apply Now
If you are an experienced Engineer looking to apply your expertise to a once-in-a-generation national program, we encourage you to apply today. Please submit your current resume. Shortlisted candidates may be asked for a short statement (up to 600 words) on how their skills, knowledge and experience fit their chosen discipline.

At Chandler Macleod, we are committed to fostering a diverse workforce where everyone is welcome. We encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, women, neurodiverse individuals, people living with a disability, and the LGBTIQA+ community. You can read more about our commitment to diversity and inclusion at: https://www.chandlermacleod.com/diversity-and-inclusion.

job.title: Haul Truck Operator
job.description:
Competitive hourly rates + super paid on all hours worked
8/6 roster | FIFO from Cairns & Darwin to Gove, NT
Opportunity working at Rio Tinto at Gove, Northern Territory

About the Opportunity
Rio Tinto is a global mining and materials company operating in 35 countries, producing the materials essential to modern life. Their operations are built on safety, innovation, inclusion and creating value for communities, customers and shareholders.

Through Rio Tinto's partnership with Chandler Macleod, we are seeking an experienced CAT 777 Dump Truck Operator to support day-to-day mining operations in the Gove region, NT.

job.title: Planner
job.description:
Planner – Participant Safeguarding Advisory Team
  • Canberra, Adelaide, Brisbane, Melbourne, Perth, Sydney or Hobart
  • $61.86 per hour plus super
  • January start date until 31 December 2027 – with potential to extend
     

The why.
We are recruiting experienced Planners to join a national Safeguarding Advisory Team focused on supporting people with disability through specialised safeguarding advice, risk assessment and intervention support.
This is a rewarding opportunity to contribute to meaningful outcomes for participants by providing expert advice, managing complex safeguarding matters and supporting frontline staff in navigating sensitive and high-risk situations.


What’s in it for you?
  • Potential career progression within this high-profile federal government agency
  • Fast paced and dynamic environment
  • Great onboarding experience with a diverse and inclusive team culture.
  • Hybrid and flexible working arrangement
  • Weekly pay cycle
  • $61.86 per hour
  • January start date until 31 December 2027 – with potential to extend

The company.
As a Planner within the Safeguarding Advisory Team, you will be responsible for assessing complex participant circumstances, identifying risks, and providing specialised safeguarding advice to support positive participant outcomes.
Working within a collaborative national team, you will partner with internal stakeholders and external agencies to coordinate safeguarding activities, deliver interventions, and contribute to continuous improvement initiatives that strengthen safeguarding practices across the organisation

The responsibility.
  • Undertake risk identification and assessment of complex and sensitive participant situations.

job.title: Chief Executive Officer
job.description:
Lead the Future of the Harvey Region

Situated between Perth and Bunbury, the Shire of Harvey is home to more than 32,000 residents and combines a thriving economy with an enviable Southwest lifestyle. With strong population growth, diverse industries and communities, significant development opportunities and a highly engaged community, the Shire offers a rare opportunity for an exceptional leader to shape the future of a region defined by growth, opportunity and quality of life.

The Shire of Harvey offers more than a leadership role. It provides the opportunity to lead within an organisation that values integrity, collaboration and continuous improvement. Supported by a strong organisational culture, professional development opportunities, employee wellbeing initiatives and a commitment to work-life balance, the Shire is focused on attracting and retaining high-performing leaders who are passionate about delivering lasting outcomes for their communities.

Joining the Shire of Harvey is more than a career opportunity. It is an opportunity to become part of a vibrant and welcoming community that values connection, contribution and shared success. The region's strong community spirit, rich natural environment and commitment to growth create a rewarding setting for leaders who are motivated by purpose, enjoy building relationships and are passionate about creating positive outcomes for the people and places they serve. The ideal candidate will embrace the opportunity to become an active and visible member of the community, sharing a genuine passion for the region, its people and its future, and fostering strong connections that help shape lasting outcomes.

Link https://harveyregion.com.au/
 

The Opportunity

Reporting directly to Council, the Chief Executive Officer will provide strategic leadership, organisational stewardship and operational management of the Shire. The CEO will lead the implementation of Council's vision and priorities while ensuring the delivery of sustainable community outcomes, major infrastructure projects, responsible financial management and exemplary governance practices.
Key priorities include:
  • Leading the delivery of Council's Council Plan 2025 – 2035
  • Driving major infrastructure, planning and development initiatives that support growth and economic prosperity.
  • Building a high-performing and customer-focused organisational culture.
  • Ensuring robust governance, accountability and legislative compliance.
  • Develop and strengthen relationships with Councillors, community members, government agencies and industry stakeholders.
  • Maintain and improve the Shire's long-term financial sustainability and organisational performance.
 
About You

We are seeking an accomplished Chief Executive Officer with a demonstrated ability to lead complex organisations and deliver strategic outcomes.
You will bring:
  • Proven experience as a Chief Executive Officer within local government, the public sector or another complex service-based organisation.
  • Strong governance and political acumen, with experience working effectively with Boards, Councils and governing bodies.
  • Experience leading major infrastructure, planning, development or growth initiatives.
  • Outstanding stakeholder engagement and relationship management capability.
  • Strong commercial and financial leadership skills.
  • A genuine commitment to community outcomes, organisational culture and public value.
 
Why Harvey?

This is a unique opportunity to lead one of the fastest growing regional local governments in Western Australia at a time of significant opportunity and transformation. With an engaged Council, ambitious strategic agenda, major infrastructure opportunities and an exceptional quality of life, the Shire of Harvey offers a rewarding leadership role where you can make a genuine and lasting impact.

Set between the coast and countryside, the Shire offers an enviable lifestyle supported by excellent community infrastructure, including 16 schools, four libraries, recreation and aquatic centres, comprehensive health services, diverse housing options and convenient retail amenities. Residents enjoy 42 kilometres of coastline, extensive parks and open spaces, a vibrant calendar of community events, a wide range of sporting and community clubs, and an outstanding selection of cafés, restaurants and local produce, making Harvey an ideal place to live, work and raise a family.
 
 
Salary Package

A negotiable remuneration package, aligned with Local Government Band 2 requirements, will be offered to the successful candidate.
 
Application Process

Closing date: 17th November 2026

To submit your application, please provide a current resume and a cover letter of no more than two pages outlining your suitability for the role.

Applications can be made by clicking apply.

A candidate information pack is available here:

https://irp.cdn-website.com/0ba2c165/files/uploaded/Candidate+Pack+-+Shire+of+Harvey+-+Chief+Executive+Final.pdf

Enquiries: For a confidential discussion on the role, you may contact Craig Moffat at Chandler Macleod on 0447 571 643.

Chandler Macleod is seeking a Mechanical Engineer for a growing mining equipment business based in Rutherford, in the Newcastle/Hunter region.

• Fluency in English and Mandarin is essential, as the role involves regular technical collaboration with engineering colleagues in China.

job.title: Project Manager
job.description:
Project Manager
Beresfield, NSW | Up to $95/hr Casual | Hybrid Working Available

Our client is a well-established leader in the mechanical services sector, delivering complex projects across water utilities and industrial environments. Due to continued growth and a strong project pipeline, an opportunity has become available for an experienced Project Manager to join their Beresfield Service Centre.

This is a hands-on role that will suit a driven and capable project professional who enjoys taking ownership, managing stakeholder relationships, and ensuring successful project delivery from initiation through to completion.

About the Role
Reporting directly to the Service Centre Manager, you will play a key role in the delivery of major water infrastructure projects, with an initial focus on Sydney Water projects while also supporting the delivery of other client works as they are secured.

You will act as the primary point of contact for clients and work closely with internal teams, subcontractors, suppliers, and site personnel to ensure projects are delivered safely, efficiently, and commercially.

  • Develop and maintain project programmes and schedules
  • Support mobilisation planning, including accommodation and logistics arrangements

About You
To be successful in this role, you will be an experienced Project Manager with a proven ability to manage multiple stakeholders, drive project outcomes, and take full ownership of project delivery.

You will ideally bring:
  • Demonstrated experience in project management within an industrial, mechanical, engineering, or utilities environment
  • Strong contract administration and commercial management capabilities
  • Experience managing project schedules, budgets, reporting, and claims
  • Excellent communication and stakeholder engagement skills
  • The confidence and capability to work autonomously and take responsibility for project outcomes
  • Mechanical industry experience
  • Water utilities experience

What's on Offer

  • Hybrid working arrangements with a minimum of 2 days per week in the office

job.title: Internal Sales & Account Management
job.description:
We are seeking a commercially minded and personable Internal Sales & Account Management to join an established plant and equipment hire business based in Dandenong South.

This is a hands-on, phone-based role focused on maintaining strong client relationships and generating dry hire opportunities across the civil and construction industries.

A large part of your day will involve proactively contacting existing and previous clients, keeping the business front of mind and understanding their upcoming projects and equipment requirements. You'll also manage inbound hire enquiries, prepare and follow up quotes, re-engage dormant clients and identify opportunities to develop new business.

There is a genuine sales element to the role, so you'll need to be comfortable picking up the phone, starting conversations and asking for the business. However, this isn't a traditional BDM position focused solely on cold acquisition or being out on the road.

Working within a small, close-knit team, you'll also be someone who is happy to jump in and assist with incoming calls and general client enquiries when needed.


Key Responsibilities
  • Proactively contact existing, previous and prospective clients to generate hire opportunities
  • Build and maintain relationships with clients across the civil and construction sectors
  • Re-engage dormant clients and identify upcoming projects or equipment requirements
  • Manage inbound hire enquiries via phone and email
  • Prepare quotes and proactively follow up outstanding opportunities
  • Identify and approach prospective clients where appropriate
  • Promote available equipment to maximise fleet utilisation
  • Maintain accurate client and sales activity within HubSpot CRM
  • Assist with incoming calls and general client enquiries across the office when required
  • Conduct phone and Microsoft Teams meetings, with occasional site visits where beneficial
  • Work closely with the wider team to maintain client engagement and sales momentum

About You
We're looking for someone who genuinely enjoys speaking with clients and is comfortable with the commercial side of relationship building.

You'll ideally be:
  • Confident making proactive outbound calls and asking clients about upcoming requirements
  • Personable, genuine and able to build rapport quickly
  • Commercially minded and comfortable identifying sales opportunities
  • Comfortable approaching new clients as well as working with established relationships
  • Persistent with follow-ups without being overly pushy
  • Reliable, consistent and willing to get involved wherever needed
  • Organised and disciplined with quotes, follow-ups and CRM activity
  • Comfortable working autonomously within a small office environment
  • Looking for a stable, long-term opportunity where you can become a valued part of the team

Experience within plant and equipment hire, earthmoving, civil construction, construction or a related industry will be highly regarded. Strong internal sales, hire or client relationship experience from another industry will also be considered.


What's on Offer
  • $80,000–$85,000 + super
  • Permanent, full-time opportunity
  • Dandenong South location
  • 100% office-based, with occasional site visits
  • Small, close-knit and down-to-earth team
  • Established client relationships to build upon
  • A varied mix of client relationships, hire coordination and proactive sales
  • Stable, long-term opportunity within an established business

job.title: FP&A Manager
job.description:
Commercial FP&A Manager, ANZ | Growing Biotech

This is a fast-growing biotech business in the middle of a global expansion. They need a finance partner who sits inside the commercial engine, not behind it. You’ll work directly with the ANZ leadership and sales teams, own the full FP&A cycle, and use it to shape how the business grows, prices and invests.

A big part of the role is working hand in hand with sales. You’ll get to know the seasonal patterns that drive demand, understand what’s behind the peaks and troughs, and turn that into forecasts the business can plan around. As the company scales into new markets, getting this right matters more every quarter.

This is a lean, growing business, so your work is visible and your input counts. Leadership will come to you when they need to understand the numbers and decide what to do next. That takes clear insight, practical forecasting and the confidence to push back when something doesn’t stack up.

What you’ll be doing

  • Partner with senior leaders and the sales team on performance and growth
  • Work closely with sales to understand seasonal cycles and build them into accurate, practical forecasts
  • Own budgeting, forecasting and monthly performance reporting across ANZ
  • Explain revenue, margin, cost and working capital results in plain commercial terms
  • Build scenario models to support pricing, investment and expansion decisions
  • Build and improve forecasting models and reporting from the ground up, using Xero and Excel
  • Find smarter ways to automate reporting and give leadership better visibility as the business scales
What you’ll bring

  • 5+ years in finance, with strong FP&A experience
  • Hands-on business partnering with sales or commercial teams
  • Experience forecasting in a business with seasonal or cyclical demand (highly regarded)
  • Advanced Excel and strong modelling skills, with Power BI or similar a plus
  • Experience with Xero or similar cloud accounting platforms
  • A hands-on approach and comfort building things without a big team or established systems around you
  • The confidence to influence senior leaders and work through ambiguity

We are currently seeking process workers to join Baiada’s team in their live bay area at the Beresfield processing facility. This facility is designed to meet the highest standards of food safety and quality, whilst also ensuring the welfare of their chickens and turkeys.

job.title: Process Operator
job.description:
Process Operator – Rio Tinto (Bell Bay Smelter, TAS)
  • Competitive hourly rate + super paid on all hours worked
  • 12-hour day/night roster | Residential / DIDO / FIFO from Bell Bay, TAS
  • Opportunity to work onsite with Rio Tinto at Bell Bay Smelter
About the Opportunity

Rio Tinto is a global mining and materials company operating in 35 countries, producing the materials essential to modern life. Their operations are built on safety, innovation, inclusion and creating value for communities, customers and shareholders.

Through Rio Tinto’s partnership with Chandler Macleod, we are seeking experienced Process Operators to join a safety-focused team at Bell Bay Smelter. You’ll work alongside experienced crews, supporting day-to-day operations while contributing to safe and reliable outcomes.

  • Strong manual handling capability and physical fitness
  • Ability to work in hot, dusty, high-risk environments

You will be responsible for supporting day-to-day tenancy operations, maintaining accurate records and ensuring rental administration is managed efficiently and in line with NSW legislation.

Skills and Experience
  • Minimum 3 years' experience in residential property management, rental administration, tenancy administration or community housing.

  • Strong administration, organisation and record-keeping skills.
  • Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills.
  • Experience using property management systems.

Benefits
  • 3-month contract with an immediate start available.
  • Opportunity to put your property management and tenancy administration experience to use.
  • Work with an organisation delivering housing and tenancy services to the community.

How to apply

job.title: Procurement Partner Level 5
job.description:
Procurement Partner (Level 5)

Contract Term: Initial 3-month engagement (approximately 9 November 2026 to 8 February 2027)

Extension: Potential extension subject to business requirements

We are seeking an experienced Procurement Partner (Level 5) to join a dynamic State Government procurement team based in East Perth. This is an excellent opportunity for a procurement professional with strong government procurement experience to contribute to the delivery of strategic sourcing, procurement, and contract management outcomes within a complex public sector environment.

About the Role

As the Procurement Partner, you will provide specialist procurement and contract management advice to business stakeholders, ensuring procurement activities are delivered in accordance with relevant government policies, legislation, and best practice principles. You will work collaboratively with internal clients to develop procurement strategies, manage tender processes, and support effective contract outcomes.

Key Responsibilities
  • Provide expert procurement and contract management advice to business areas.
  • Lead and manage procurement activities, including market approaches, evaluations, negotiations, and contract establishment.
  • Support stakeholders in the planning and delivery of procurement strategies and sourcing initiatives.
  • Ensure compliance with Western Australian Government procurement policies, procedures, and legislative requirements.
  • Develop and manage contract documentation, variations, and performance monitoring activities.
  • Build effective relationships with key internal and external stakeholders.
  • Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives across procurement and contract management functions.
Essential Requirements
  • Demonstrated experience in procurement and contract management within a government or large organisational environment.
  • Mandatory experience in Western Australian Government procurement processes and frameworks.
  • Strong knowledge of procurement legislation, policies, and governance requirements.
  • Excellent stakeholder engagement, negotiation, and communication skills.
  • Proven ability to manage competing priorities and deliver outcomes within tight timeframes.
Desirable Qualifications
  • Chartered Institute of Procurement & Supply (CIPS) qualification, or demonstrated progress towards obtaining CIPS accreditation.
  • Experience managing complex procurement projects and high-value contracts.
What's on Offer
  • Opportunity to contribute to a high-performing procurement function.
  • Convenient East Perth location.
  • Initial three-month engagement with the possibility of extension based on operational requirements.
  • Collaborative and professional working environment.
Candidates with strong procurement expertise and demonstrated WA Government experience are encouraged to apply. Applications should clearly outline relevant procurement and contract management experience, including exposure to government procurement frameworks and contract management practices.

job.title: Meter Reader - Metro
job.description:
Chandler Macleod is seeking expressions of interest for a number of exciting opportunities available for Gas Meter Readers to join the amazing team in the Metro area (West, North locations)

No previous experience required – training will be provided.
 
Previous experience being on your feet in physical roles will be very beneficial. 

The purpose of this role is to:

The Purpose of the Gas Meter Readers is to read electric, gas or water meters, record usage, inspect meters and connections for defects and damage, and report irregularities.
 
What we are Looking for
  • Can work independently
  • Enjoys working outdoors (rain, hail, or shine)
  • ASAP start
  • Loves fitness and has a good physical ability to walk long hours (30km a day)
  • Able to meet strict deadlines
  • Highly focused on safety with a high level of attention to detail
  • On time and reliable 
  • Valid drivers licence and access to car 
  • Highly committed and motivated
 
Responsibilities and Key Deliverables
  • Safely Navigate properties to gas meter location, avoiding hazards onsite & update hazard information for future meter readers
  • Report all encounters of gas meter leaks, damaged, vandalized, and unsafe meter installations, tampering with meters & address error
  • Entry properties to read installed gas meters & leaving the property in the state it was found
  • Ensure all dealings with the public are professional & polite
  • Ensure a high standard of personal presentation at all times & ensure to wear the supplied PPE
  • Accurately read meters for gas distributor AusNet services on behalf of gas retailers & fulfill contracted duties daily
  • Occasionally complete car-based routes that require driving onto properties to obtain reads, including along busy roads & Highways
  • Work typically starts in the field between 7am – 8am & 6:30am on the days where it is going to be over 35 degrees & must download completed work by 4:30pm each day once route has been completed
What we Offer:
  • Equipment provided
  • Training
  • Flexible ongoing full-time opportunities (available for full time hours is preferred for scheduling)
  • $34.14 per hour + super
  • Ideally you will have the flexibility to be available for up to 37.5 hours per week, training is usually full time hours and there is the possibility of being rostered for hours between 5/8 hours per day. 
Clear Drug & Alcohol test and Police Check required before placement. 

Please apply online NOW!  At Chandler Macleod, we are committed to fostering a diverse workforce where everyone is welcome. We encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, women, neurodiverse, people living with a disability and the LGBTIQA+ community.

job.title: Assistant Director – Service Delivery
job.description:
About the company:

This Federal Government agency works to deliver programs and services that support people with disability and their families, aiming to improve access, engagement, and outcomes across Australia. The agency collaborates closely with communities, service providers, and government stakeholders to implement initiatives that enhance social inclusion, wellbeing, and equity.

About the Team

The Safeguarding Advisory Team plays a critical role in supporting participant safety, risk management, and operational excellence. The team provides specialist safeguarding advice, coordinates risk-related activities, manages complex enquiries, and works collaboratively with stakeholders to achieve positive participant outcomes.
The team is committed to delivering timely, consistent, and participant-centred services while continuously improving processes, frameworks, and operational practices.

About the Role
The Agency is seeking an experienced and motivated Service Delivery Team Leader to provide leadership, strategic direction, and operational oversight within a high-performing team.
This role is responsible for leading complex pieces of work that support the delivery of quality outcomes across national service delivery functions. Working under broad direction, you will manage a team, oversee operational priorities, drive continuous improvement initiatives, and provide expert advice on complex participant and service delivery matters.
You will play a key leadership role, ensuring risks and issues are effectively managed, resources are appropriately allocated, and team outcomes align with strategic and operational objectives.

Key Responsibilities
 
  • Lead and manage a team delivering complex service delivery and safeguarding outcomes.
  • Build and maintain strong relationships with key internal and external stakeholders.
  • Provide strategic and operational advice on participant pathways, service delivery processes, and business systems.
  • Monitor, identify, and manage risks and issues that may impact organisational objectives.
  • Drive continuous improvement initiatives and support business transformation activities.
  • Oversee team workload allocation, resource management, and performance to ensure delivery of key priorities.
  • Prepare high-quality reports, briefings, and recommendations for senior leaders.
  • Lead the development and maintenance of operational guidance, procedures, and knowledge resources.
  • Represent the Agency in stakeholder forums and support negotiations where required.
  • Provide coaching, mentoring, and leadership to support team capability and performance.
  • Contribute to strategic planning, operational assurance, and safeguarding initiatives.

You Must Have
 
  • Proven experience leading teams and delivering complex operational outcomes.
  • Strong stakeholder engagement and relationship management skills.
  • Experience managing competing priorities and delivering results in a fast-paced environment.
  • Excellent communication skills, including the ability to prepare reports, briefings, and strategic recommendations.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making capabilities.
  • Experience identifying, assessing, and managing operational risks.
  • The ability to influence stakeholders and gain commitment to initiatives and outcomes.
  • Demonstrated experience driving continuous improvement and implementing process enhancements.
  • Strong planning, organisational, and resource management skills.
  • Experience coaching, developing, and supporting high-performing teams.

Benefits:
  • January start (pending Federal Police Clearance)
  • Assignment end date: 31 December 2027 with possibility of extension
  • Location:  Geelong VIC, Wollongong NSW, Parramatta NSW, Robina QLD, Adelaide CBD SA
  • $602.55 daily + Super


How to apply:

Chandler Macleod is an equal opportunity employer as part of our commitment to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people, disability and culturally and linguistics candidates are also encouraged to apply.

Please note the successful candidate for the role must hold Australian Citizenship.

Application closes on the 9th of November 2026

job.description:

Our client is a well-established and growing Australian business supplying premium aluminium façade and architectural systems to the construction industry. Due to continued growth, they are seeking an ambitious Business Development Manager to drive sales, expand market share, and contribute to their long-term success.

About the Opportunity Reporting into the leadership team, you will be responsible for identifying and developing new business opportunities, managing an existing sales pipeline, and building strong relationships across the construction sector.

The successful candidate will play a key role in growing market presence and securing project specifications with architects and builders throughout a designated territory.

With a healthy pipeline of active and pending projects already in place, you'll be responsible for maintaining momentum, converting opportunities into sales, and expanding business growth.

Key Responsibilities
  • Develop and maintain relationships with architects, builders, developers, and contractors.
  • Secure project specifications and manage opportunities through the full sales cycle.
  • Maintain and grow a strong pipeline of sales opportunities.
  • Conduct regular client meetings and site visits across your territory.
  • Collaborate with estimating and marketing teams to generate quality leads.
  • Utilise CRM systems to manage opportunities, record activity, and track performance.
  • Monitor and maintain pipeline accuracy and reporting.
  • Work closely with internal stakeholders to achieve sales and growth targets.
  • Stay informed on construction industry trends, façade systems, and architectural products.
  • Deliver exceptional customer service and contribute to long-term client retention.
About You We're looking for someone who is commercially minded, self-motivated, and passionate about sales.

Essential Requirements
  • Minimum 2 years' experience selling construction materials in a B2B environment.
  • Proven experience dealing with architects, builders, and construction stakeholders.
  • Strong understanding of the construction industry.
  • Experience using CRM systems and working to weekly KPIs.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage a sales pipeline and drive results.
  • Excellent communication, negotiation, and relationship-building skills.
  • Highly motivated, resilient, and target-driven.
  • Willingness to undertake administrative tasks as part of a small and agile team environment.

job.title: Asset Manager
job.description:
Role Overview:
We are seeking an Asset Manager to take ownership of the performance, reliability, risk profile and long-term lifecycle management of a portfolio of critical energy infrastructure assets located across Victoria, New South Wales and potentially New Zealand.
A key focus of the role will be supporting assets such as synchronous condensers and terminal stations, ensuring they continue to operate safely, efficiently and in line with operational and business objectives.
Success in this position will come from combining strong technical capability with effective stakeholder engagement, commercial awareness and a proactive approach to continuous improvement. Just as important as technical experience is a willingness to learn, accept feedback and contribute positively to the wider team.

The Opportunity:
This role will play a key part in optimising the performance and reliability of strategically important electrical infrastructure assets.
Working alongside engineering, maintenance, operations and commercial teams, you will support the development of asset strategies, oversee risk management activities, improve asset performance and help guide long-term investment decisions.
The position provides a balance of office-based work, stakeholder engagement and occasional site travel, offering exposure to both the technical and commercial aspects of asset ownership.

Key Responsibilities:
  • Drive asset performance, reliability and lifecycle outcomes across a portfolio of electrical infrastructure assets.
  • Assist in developing and implementing asset management plans and strategies.
  • Monitor asset condition, risk, performance and compliance requirements.
  • Identify and support opportunities to improve asset performance and efficiency.
  • Contribute to capital planning, budgeting and investment decisions.
  • Work collaboratively with operational, engineering and maintenance teams.
  • Support the management and mitigation of technical and commercial risks.
  • Coordinate and engage with external contractors and service providers.
  • Participate in periodic site visits across Victoria and New South Wales.
  • Contribute to the ongoing reliability and sustainability of the asset portfolio.
Skills & Experience Essential:
  • Experience within Asset Management, Asset Engineering, Reliability Engineering or Asset Performance environments.
  • Understanding of asset lifecycle and maintenance management principles.
  • Exposure to electrical, utility or infrastructure-based assets.
  • Strong stakeholder engagement and communication skills.
  • Knowledge of risk management and reliability methodologies.
  • Ability to evaluate both technical and commercial considerations.
  • Well-developed organisational and prioritisation skills.
Desirable:
  • Experience working with or around Synchronous Condensers.
  • Exposure to Terminal Station or Substation assets.
  • Transmission, power systems or broader electrical infrastructure experience.
  • Utilities, renewable energy or critical infrastructure background.
  • Exposure to HV assets and electrical networks.
  • Experience contributing to asset strategy, maintenance optimisation or investment planning activities.
About You: We're looking for someone who brings strong technical foundations, but equally demonstrates the attitude and mindset required to grow within the role.
You will ideally be someone who:
  • Takes initiative and ownership of their work.
  • Has a genuine desire to learn and develop.
  • Welcomes feedback and uses it constructively.
  • Isn't afraid to ask questions when faced with unfamiliar challenges.
  • Has a strong interest in asset performance and infrastructure reliability.
  • Is organised, accountable and dependable.
  • Can adapt to changing priorities and challenges.
  • Builds positive relationships with a wide range of stakeholders.
  • Is motivated by making assets perform better, rather than simply chasing a title.
Importantly, this opportunity is open to candidates who may be stepping into a larger Asset Management role. The focus is less on finding the most senior person and more on finding someone with the right technical foundation, attitude, growth mindset and willingness to get stuck in and develop.

Working Arrangements:
  • Permanent full-time opportunity.
  • Hybrid model with 3 days in the office and 2 days working remotely.
  • Initial onboarding period will be office-based.
  • Approximately 1-2 site visits per month.
  • Travel across Victoria and New South Wales as required.
  • Potential future travel to New Zealand.
