job.title: Senior Commissioning Engineer
job.description:
Senior Commissioning Engineer Permanent Role | Major HV & Power Infrastructure Projects | Melbourne / VIC

A leading Australian power and energy infrastructure organisation is seeking an experienced Senior Commissioning Engineer to join their team.

This role is ideally suited to a commissioning professional with strong experience operating within regulated electricity network environments and a background in testing, commissioning, protection systems, energisation and utility infrastructure.
Working across projects up to 500kV, you will take ownership of commissioning activities from planning and testing through to energisation and final handover.

The Opportunity: You will play a key role in the delivery of critical electrical infrastructure, supporting large-scale transmission, distribution, renewable energy, data centre and network infrastructure projects.
The successful candidate will be responsible for the testing, commissioning and energisation of primary and secondary systems while ensuring compliance with utility standards, safety requirements and operational frameworks.

Key Responsibilities:
Testing & Commissioning (Senior Level)
  • Lead HV testing and commissioning activities on primary plant from 415V through to 500kV.
  • Perform secondary injection testing across a broad range of protection schemes.
  • Test protection relays, control systems, SCADA and communications platforms.
  • Integrate AC and DC control systems in both greenfield and brownfield environments.
  • Review designs and drawings to validate protection schemes and constructability.
  • Apply, verify and modify IED settings using OEM software.
  • Develop commissioning methodologies, test plans, ITPs and acceptance documentation.
  • Support energisation programs, outage activities and operational handovers.
Highly Regarded Qualifications:

Candidates holding any of the following will be viewed favourably:
  • Advanced Diploma of ESI (Power Systems)
  • Electrical Engineering Degree
  • Protection & Control qualifications
  • HV Switching Authorisations
  • Senior Authorised Person experience
  • Utility competency programs
  • Network access competencies
  • Utility-specific authorisations and approvals
Candidates holding an Advanced Diploma of ESI (Power Systems), HV Switching Authorisations, utility network competencies or previous experience working within regulated network environments are strongly encouraged to apply.

Utility & Network Experience:

Candidates with experience operating within regulated electricity network environments are strongly encouraged to apply.
We are particularly interested in professionals who can demonstrate:

  • Provide accurate market intelligence and business development reporting.

Essential Skills & Experience
  • Minimum 5 years' experience in steel sales, construction materials sales, building products, or a related industry.

job.title: Manager, Research Contracts
job.description:
Manager, Research Contracts | $94.11 p/h + Super | Melbourne CBD
Hybrid Working | University Environment | Immediate Start | Potential Extension

We are currently seeking an experienced Manager, Research Contracts to join a leading university based in Melbourne CBD.

This is an excellent opportunity for a commercially minded professional with strong contract law knowledge, negotiation skills and the ability to navigate complex contractual arrangements.

We welcome applications from experienced contracts professionals, legal practitioners and internationally qualified lawyers currently residing in Melbourne who are looking to utilise their legal expertise within the Australian workforce.

The OpportunityReporting to the Senior Manager, Research Contracts, you will be responsible for reviewing, drafting and negotiating a broad range of commercial and research-related agreements.

These agreements may include research funding arrangements, collaborative research partnerships, intellectual property licensing and commercial research contracts.

Working closely with internal legal, finance and risk teams, as well as external funding bodies and industry partners, you will provide commercially sound advice, manage contractual risks and facilitate successful outcomes.

This position offers a high degree of autonomy within a collaborative university environment.


Key Responsibilities
  • Review, draft and negotiate commercial contracts, research agreements, funding arrangements and collaborative partnerships.
  • Assess contractual risks relating to intellectual property, insurance, indemnities and compliance obligations.
  • Provide practical commercial and contractual advice to internal stakeholders.
  • Negotiate contractual terms with external funding agencies, research collaborators and industry partners.
  • Collaborate with legal, finance and risk teams to ensure agreements comply with organisational policies.
  • Identify potential contractual risks and recommend commercially viable solutions.
  • Prepare recommendations to support informed decisions regarding contract execution.
  • Maintain accurate contractual documentation, records and reporting.
  • Contribute to continuous improvement across contract management processes.

About You
We are seeking a professional with strong legal knowledge, commercial awareness and the confidence to interpret and negotiate complex agreements.
Ideally, you will demonstrate:
  • A relevant tertiary qualification in Law, Business, Commerce or a related discipline, or equivalent experience.
  • Sound knowledge of contract law, contractual obligations and commercial risk management.
  • Experience drafting, reviewing, interpreting or negotiating contracts and legal agreements.
  • An understanding of intellectual property, indemnities, insurance provisions and contractual risk.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to recommend commercially sound solutions.
  • Excellent communication and stakeholder engagement skills.
  • Strong negotiation capabilities and the ability to manage competing priorities.
  • The ability to work independently and exercise sound professional judgement.

Internationally qualified lawyers are encouraged to apply.

We recognise that legal professionals who have obtained their qualifications or practised overseas often possess highly transferable skills and a strong foundation in contract law.

If you are an overseas-qualified lawyer currently residing in Melbourne and working towards recognition of your qualifications in Australia, this may be an excellent opportunity to apply your existing legal knowledge in a commercial contracting environment.

Previous experience in research contracts, government, higher education or complex commercial environments will be highly regarded but is not essential.


Position Details
  • Location: Melbourne CBD
  • Hourly Rate: $94.11 per hour + superannuation
  • Hours: 36 hours per week, full-time
  • Contract Duration: ASAP to 23 December 2026
  • Extension: Potential for extension
  • Working Arrangements: Hybrid, minimum 2 days on-site per week, with Thursday as the designated anchor day

Essential Requirements
  • Must currently reside in Melbourne and have valid Australian working rights.
  • Must hold or be willing and eligible to obtain a valid Victorian Employee Working with Children Check.
  • Ability to commence at short notice is highly desirable.

Interested?
If you have a strong foundation in contract law and commercial agreements and are looking for an opportunity to apply your expertise within a university environment, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply Now to submit your CV for consideration.

job.title: Requirements Management and Analysis Technical Specialist
job.description:
Chandler Macleod is recruiting on behalf of our client for an exceptional opportunity within a high-profile Federal Government agency supporting Australia’s most significant long-term capability program.

This is a unique chance for an experienced APS6 Requirements Management and Analysis Technical Specialist to support the Australian Submarine Agency (ASA), contributing to a nationally significant defence initiative that will shape Australia’s security, workforce, industrial capability and supply chains for decades to come.

About the Role

Working within the Australian Submarine Agency environment, the Requirements Management and Analysis Technical Specialist (APS6) is accountable (under broad direction and with a high degree of autonomy) for providing technical expertise, systems administration support, analysis and stakeholder engagement to enable effective requirements management and Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) practices.

The acquisition of conventionally-armed, nuclear-powered submarines is an historic and transformative endeavour for Australia. This whole-of-nation effort will transform Australia’s economic and national security landscape for decades to come.

You will support the governance, implementation, continuous improvement and user adoption of the Requirements Management System (RMS) and associated engineering toolsets, ensuring requirements, architectures, design artefacts and traceability information are managed in accordance with organisational standards and systems engineering best practice.

About the Team

The Requirements Analysis and Intelligence Directorate provides analytical and intelligence support to the Capability Sponsor within the ASA. The directorate enables informed and evidence-based decision-making by supporting the development, management, governance and assurance of capability requirements throughout the capability lifecycle.
The directorate’s functions align with the principles of a nuclear mindset through a commitment to technical excellence, procedural compliance, accountability, traceability, a questioning attitude and continuous learning.

Key Responsibilities

You will be responsible for supporting and delivering requirements management and MBSE outcomes, including:
  • Providing technical expertise and system administration support for the RMS and associated engineering tools
  • Supporting governance, implementation, continuous improvement and user adoption of requirements and MBSE practices
  • Applying systems engineering principles to support the development, management, traceability, verification and analysis of requirements across the capability lifecycle
  • Supporting stakeholders in the development, maintenance and effective use of system models (MBSE)
  • Conducting and presenting evidence-based analysis to support informed decision-making (including identification of trends, risks, impacts and opportunities)
  • Troubleshooting technical issues and developing practical solutions in a complex stakeholder environment
  • Translating technical concepts for non-technical audiences through clear written and verbal communication
  • Managing competing priorities and delivering outcomes in a fast-paced, high-profile environment
About You
You will demonstrate:
  • Experience applying systems engineering principles and requirements management practices across a capability lifecycle
  • Familiarity with MBSE approaches and tools, and the ability to support stakeholders using them effectively
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with a track record of practical delivery
  • Strong stakeholder engagement capability, including communicating complex technical concepts clearly
  • Ability to manage competing priorities and deliver outcomes under pressure
Mandatory qualifications / experience (required)
  • A degree in Engineering (any specialisation), Mathematics, Data Analysis, Computer Science, Physics or Science, or a related discipline
Security Requirement 
  • Applicants must be able to obtain and maintain a Negative Vetting Level 1 (NV1) security clearance
  • Flexible working arrangements may be supported where aligned with operational and business requirements
Apply Now

If you are an experienced requirements management / MBSE professional seeking to contribute to a once-in-a-lifetime national program, we encourage you to apply today.

You will be responsible for leading and delivering complex analytical activities, including:

job.title: Study Manager
job.description:
Chandler Macleod is partnering with a well-established, large-scale organisation in the resources / heavy industry space to recruit an experienced Study Manager to lead a major greenfield Concept Study (FEL1). This is a key appointment as the project pipeline grows, offering the chance to influence early investment decisions and shape the definition of a significant future program of work.

This role will suit someone who is confident operating in ambiguity, comfortable facilitating alignment (without losing objectivity), and experienced producing decision-quality study outcomes for senior stakeholders.

The Opportunity

As Study Manager, you will establish and lead the early-phase study approach—bringing disciplined study and project management practices to test strategic fit, technical viability, value, risk, and execution pathways before material capital is committed. You’ll work across a complex, evolving environment with multiple internal and external interfaces, coordinating multidisciplinary inputs and ensuring study recommendations are supported by clear evidence, transparent assumptions, and fit-for-purpose governance.

Key responsibilities

Health, safety and environment
  • Provide visible leadership and ensure study delivery aligns with HSE requirements, policies and critical risk controls.
Study planning & delivery (FEL1 and potentially FEL2–3)
  • Define the study strategy, scope, objectives, deliverables, basis of study and execution plan
  • Lead an integrated team to deliver study outputs safely, on time and within budget
  • Build and maintain realistic schedules, resource plans, budgets and forecasts (including forward estimates for subsequent phases)
Business case development
  • Develop commercially relevant, decision-ready business cases assessing:
    • options and trade-offs
    • costs, schedule, value drivers and key assumptions
    • risks, opportunities and sustainability impacts
    • execution and implementation pathways
Options / trade-off analysis
  • Structure and facilitate workshops and working sessions for:
    • opportunity framing
    • optioneering / range analysis
    • trade-off decision making
  • Ensure options are evaluated consistently and recommendations are traceable to agreed criteria.
Risk, assurance and governance
  • Maintain risk, opportunity, assumptions and decision registers
  • Coordinate peer reviews / technical reviews / independent assurance and close out actions
  • Provide concise reporting on progress, cost, schedule, risk, decisions and required interventions
Stakeholder management
  • Engage across operational, technical, commercial and corporate stakeholder groups
  • Build strong working relationships with senior leaders and external parties
  • Lead decision forums and stakeholder workshops to create alignment while preserving constructive challenge
External service providers
  • Develop scopes of work, support procurement, and manage consultants/service providers to meet safety, quality, cost and schedule expectations.
About you (selection criteria)

To be successful in this role, you will bring a strong blend of study leadership, stakeholder influence, and delivery discipline.

Essential
  • Demonstrated experience delivering early-phase Concept and/or Pre-Feasibility studies in mining, minerals processing, heavy industry, manufacturing or comparable sectors
  • Strong study/project management capability with an ability to lead multidisciplinary inputs
  • Proven experience managing complex stakeholder groups, including senior executives and external parties
  • Well-developed written and verbal communication skills (reports, executive papers, presentations, workshops)
  • Relevant tertiary qualification (engineering, metallurgy, chemistry, project management, business or related) or extensive equivalent industry experience
  • Willingness and ability to travel to site as required
Highly regarded
  • 15+ years’ experience across resources / heavy industry development, studies or major projects
  • Exposure to complex processing operations (e.g., refineries, concentrators, smelters or similar)
  • Formal project/study management training and/or recognised certification
  • Experience facilitating structured processes such as range analysis, opportunity framing and optioneering
  • Risk management / process safety / technical assurance experience
  • Financial/economic evaluation capability (investment concepts, valuation/NPV modelling, business case assessment)
What’s on offer
  • Location Perth (Hybrid)
  • Roster Monday to Friday
  • Contract term 6–12 months initially (project-driven; extension possible)
  • Start date ASAP
  • Rate Approx. $150/hr + super (negotiable for the right person)
If you have a strong early-phase study background and are looking for a role where you can lead a high-profile greenfield concept program, apply now with your CV.

job.title: Regional Manager
job.description:
We are seeking an experienced and commercially astute Regional Manager to take full ownership of a leading heavy vehicle and transport solutions operation, driving sales growth, workshop performance, parts operations, customer relationships, and overall branch profitability.

This is a unique opportunity for a hands-on leader who understands the heavy vehicle industry from the ground up. Two opportunities are available, located in Sydney and Brisbane.

Who We're Looking For

We're seeking a genuine industry leader who has progressed from a hands-on workshop or production environment into senior management. You understand the operational realities of a heavy vehicle, manufacturing, or service-based business and combine this experience with strong commercial acumen, customer relationship management skills, and a proven ability to lead high-performing teams while driving sustainable business growth and profitability.

About the Role

Reporting to senior leadership, you will have full responsibility for the strategic and operational performance of your state operation.

With complete P&L accountability, you will oversee:

• New and used equipment sales
• Workshop service, repairs and maintenance operations
• Spare parts sales and inventory management
• Customer service and after-sales support
• Safety, compliance and facility management
• Team leadership, coaching and performance

This role requires a balance of commercial acumen and operational leadership, with the ability to move seamlessly between customer meetings, sales strategy, workshop operations, and financial management.

What You'll Bring

Essential Experience
5+ years' experience leading a branch, region or business unit within:
• Heavy vehicles
• Transport equipment
• Manufacturing
• Automotive OEM
• Truck or equipment servicing operations
• Strong commercial and financial management capability
• Proven leadership experience with direct P&L responsibility
• Demonstrated success managing customer relationships and driving revenue growth
• Experience leading workshop and operational teams
Highly Desirable
• Trade qualification in Diesel Mechanics, Fabrication, Welding or a related discipline
• Experience within the heavy vehicle, transport equipment or manufacturing sectors
• Understanding of heavy vehicle repairs, maintenance and aftermarket parts operations
• Existing network across transport, logistics or fleet customers

Success in This Role Looks Like

• Achieving branch EBIT and profitability targets
• Growing equipment sales and market share
• Improving workshop productivity and turnaround times
• Expanding parts revenue and inventory performance
• Delivering exceptional customer outcomes
• Building an engaged, accountable and high-performing team

Why Join?

• Lead a significant state operation within a well-established industry leader
• Genuine autonomy with full state responsibility
• Executive-level influence and visibility
• Strong support from a national leadership team
• Opportunity to drive growth and shape the future of the business
• Competitive salary package including vehicle and incentive structure

Apply Now

If you've come from the workshop floor, understand the transport industry, and have developed into a commercially driven business leader, we'd love to hear from you.

Submit your resume and cover letter via the Apply Now link.

We currently have two opportunities available, based in Sydney and Brisbane.

For a copy of the Position Description or a confidential discussion about either role, please contact Jo Ellerman on (02) 6691 9106.

Key Responsibilities
  • Assess engineering components of Development Applications (DAs), Subdivision Works Certificates and Subdivision Certificates.

  • Prepare assessment reports, engineering conditions and recommendations within required timeframes.

About You
You will be a highly experienced Civil Engineer with a strong background in land development, subdivision projects and development assessment.

Essential Requirements
  • Degree in Civil Engineering.
  • Current NSW Class C Driver Licence.
  • Extensive experience in development engineering, civil design and construction associated with urban development.
  • Strong knowledge of roads, drainage, stormwater, flooding, traffic and water quality management principles.
  • Experience assessing Development Applications, Subdivision Works Certificates and Subdivision Certificates.
  • Knowledge of the Environmental Planning & Assessment Act 1979 and related legislation.
  • Excellent stakeholder engagement, negotiation and problem-solving skills.
Highly Regarded
  • Local Government development engineering experience.
  • Land subdivision expertise.
  • Postgraduate qualifications in Civil Engineering or a related discipline.
  • Working knowledge of the Local Government Act and Roads Act.

Heritage Concrete is a growing concreting business based in Uralla, NSW. With a strong reputation for quality workmanship and reliable delivery, the team works across a range of concrete projects and is looking to appoint a new Leading Hand Concreter / Site Coordinator to support continued growth.

This is a newly created role for an experienced concreter who enjoys being hands-on onsite while also taking responsibility for coordinating people, projects and day-to-day operations.

For the right candidate, relocation assistance is on offer, providing the opportunity to join a respected regional business and play a key role in its continued growth.


About the Role
This is a practical, hands-on role where approximately 90% of your time will be spent onsite managing and delivering concreting projects, while also supporting the coordination and administration required to keep jobs running smoothly.

You will work closely with the business owners, clients, contractors and team members to ensure projects are well planned, organised and completed to a high standard.

The role will suit someone who enjoys being on the tools but also has the communication skills and organisational ability to coordinate jobs from start to finish.


Key Responsibilities
  • Lead and support concreting teams onsite to deliver quality outcomes
  • Coordinate daily site activities, resources and workflow
  • Work alongside the team as a hands-on concreter when required
  • Liaise with clients, contractors and suppliers to ensure clear communication
  • Support job planning, scheduling and progress tracking
  • Coordinate materials, equipment and purchasing requirements
  • Track purchase orders and ensure materials are available when needed
  • Assist with quality control and ensuring work meets project requirements
  • Provide updates, manage expectations and resolve day-to-day issues onsite
  • Support project coordination between the site team and office

About You
You are an experienced concreter who enjoys taking ownership and making sure jobs run smoothly.

You will ideally have:
  • Solid experience in concreting and civil/construction environments
  • The ability to confidently lead and coordinate a team onsite
  • Strong practical knowledge of concrete processes, materials and sequencing
  • Good organisation skills and the ability to manage multiple priorities
  • Strong communication skills with clients, contractors and team members
  • A proactive approach and willingness to get involved wherever needed
  • The ability to balance hands-on trade work with planning and coordination

Experience managing projects, crews or subcontractors will be highly regarded.


What’s on Offer
  • Permanent full-time opportunity

job.title: Material and Logistics Officer
job.description:
About the Company Join a leading organisation dedicated to decarbonisation projects within the energy and resources sector. Focused on sustainable initiatives, this company is at the forefront of reducing environmental impact and driving innovative solutions to power a cleaner future. Based in Perth, it’s a dynamic place to grow your career while contributing to meaningful change.

About the Role We’re currently looking for a Material and Logistics Officer to support our decarbonisation projects. The role has become available due to ongoing project expansion and the need for dedicated professionals to keep things running smoothly from procurement to delivery. Reporting to the Project Manager – Procurement, you'll be crucial in coordinating purchasing and logistics, ensuring everything arrives on time, and maintaining efficient workflows.

Key responsibilities include:

  • Minimum of 5 years’ experience in procurement or logistics roles, ideally within a similar industry

  • Strong organisational skills with the ability to prioritise tasks and manage competing demands
  • Excellent relationship-building skills across internal and external stakeholders
  • Ability to work independently and think critically to resolve issues
  • Knowledge of health, safety, and environmental standards
  • A forklift licence is a bonus, but not essential

Why apply?
This is a fantastic chance to join a purpose-driven organisation committed to innovative sustainability projects. You’ll work in a supportive environment that values safety, integrity, and continuous improvement. Plus, enjoy the stability of a Perth-based role with the opportunity to make a real impact.

Ready to be part of something meaningful? Apply now and bring your expertise to a workplace where your contributions truly matter!

job.description:

job.title: Digital Testing Lead
job.description:
Digital Testing Lead
  • Opportunity working at Rio Tinto
  • 5-month assignment via Chandler Macleod
  • Safety-first culture with supportive teams
About the Opportunity
Rio Tinto is a global mining and materials company operating in 35 countries, producing the materials essential to modern life. Their operations are built on safety, innovation, inclusion and creating value for communities, customers and shareholders.

Through Rio Tinto’s partnership with Chandler Macleod, we are seeking an experienced Digital Testing Lead to join the Finance Digital team.

Entering the project during mid-build, the Digital Testing Lead will lead user acceptance testing for Finance Digital products and changes, making sure business users can test effectively and that the project has a clear, evidence-based view of readiness for release.

Key Responsibilities
  • Plan and coordinate UAT activities with business representatives, product owners and the delivery team.
  • Define test scenarios, test cases and acceptance criteria with the relevant business users.
  • Prepare testers, coordinate testing sessions and keep the test schedule on track.
  • Record, prioritise and follow up defects, issues and decisions arising through UAT.
  • Work with delivery and technical teams to ensure defects are understood, resolved and retested.
  • Provide clear reporting on test progress, outstanding risks and readiness for release.
  • Maintain UAT evidence, including test outcomes, defect status and business sign-off.
  • Identify gaps in test coverage or business readiness early and escalate them appropriately.

To be successful in this role, you encompass;
  • Experience leading or coordinating UAT in a business, finance, systems or digital-delivery environment.
  • Able to work comfortably with business users who have varying levels of technical confidence.
  • Strong organisation and follow-through across multiple testers, scenarios and competing priorities.
  • Clear written communication, particularly for defects, risks, test outcomes and release-readiness reporting.
  • Can demonstrate practical judgement about what needs escalation and what can be resolved within the delivery team.
  • Experience with the SAP Analytic Cloud (SAC) and SAP Business Data Cloud (BDC) will be highly regarded but not critical.

Apply now!
 If you are organised, calm under pressure and prepared to seek clarification when testing outcomes are unclear, we would love to hear from you.

job.title: Audit and Assurance Officer
job.description:
Chandler Macleod is recruiting on behalf of our client for an experienced Audit & Assurance Officer to support governance, risk, audit and business continuity functions within a Federal Government environment. This is an excellent opportunity for a governance professional with strong audit, assurance and stakeholder engagement experience to contribute to organisational resilience and continuous improvement initiatives.

  • Locations: Albury NSW, Griffith NSW,  Canberra ACT, Goondiwindi QLD, Mildura VIC, Adelaide SA , Murray Bridge SA,
  • Contract: 12-month contract with potential extension
  • Work Arrangement: Flexible working arrangements may be considered

About the Role
As the APS 6 Audit & Assurance Officer, you will play a key role in coordinating internal audit programs, supporting assurance and risk management activities, maintaining governance frameworks, and contributing to business continuity planning. You will work closely with senior stakeholders, governance committees, external providers and business areas to strengthen organisational performance and compliance.

Key Responsibilities
  • Coordinate and manage the delivery of internal audits, including planning, stakeholder engagement, audit monitoring and reporting.
  • Maintain audit recommendation registers, track management actions and provide timely reporting to leadership and governance committees.
  • Manage relationships with internal audit service providers and support assurance, compliance and risk management activities.
  • Prepare high-quality reports, briefings and committee papers relating to audit, risk, assurance and business continuity.
  • Contribute to the continuous improvement of governance, risk and assurance frameworks, policies and processes.
  • Support business continuity planning, testing activities and organisational resilience initiatives.
  • Coordinate external reviews, risk workshops and assurance activities as required.

About You To be successful in this role, you will demonstrate:

  • Experience in audit, assurance, risk management, governance or compliance within a complex organisation.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to identify trends, risks and improvement opportunities.
  • Excellent written communication skills, including experience preparing reports, briefings and executive-level documentation.
  • Proven ability to manage competing priorities and deliver outcomes within tight timeframes.
  • Strong stakeholder engagement and relationship management skills.
  • Experience supporting governance committees and working with senior leaders.
  • Knowledge of business continuity frameworks and organisational resilience practices will be highly regarded.
  • Experience within a Federal Government environment is desirable.

job.title: Senior Manager Communication and Engagement
job.description:
Chandler Macleod is recruiting on behalf of our client for an experienced Senior Manager Communication & Engagement to lead strategic community engagement and stakeholder communication activities across a nationally significant infrastructure program.

This senior leadership opportunity will see you driving engagement strategies, managing complex stakeholder relationships, leading a high-performing team, and ensuring community feedback is effectively integrated into project planning and delivery. The role plays a critical part in building trust, maintaining social licence, and supporting the successful delivery of major infrastructure outcomes. 
  • Contract: 12-month contract with potential extension
  • Locations: Location: Sydney, Canberra, Newcastle OR Central Coast
  • Work Arrangement: 
    • On-site role with flexible work arrangements to balance operational and team needs.
    • Regular travel across project locations and other HSRA offices. Some evening and weekend work will be required to support engagement activities and operational commitments.

About the Role
Reporting to the General Manager, Project Communication, you will provide strategic leadership across communication and engagement activities within a designated project region. You will oversee engagement programs, manage sensitive stakeholder matters, and guide teams through complex community, property and construction-related issues.
This role requires a highly experienced communications professional who can operate confidently in politically sensitive environments while delivering outstanding stakeholder outcomes.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Leadership
  • Lead the development and execution of communication and community engagement strategies aligned to organisational objectives.
  • Provide expert advice on complex stakeholder, community and project-related matters.
  • Manage and mentor an experienced team of engagement professionals.
  • Drive continuous improvement, governance and compliance across engagement activities.
  • Contribute to strategic planning and organisational priorities.

Stakeholder Engagement & Communications
  • Build and maintain strong relationships with community members, landowners, government agencies and key stakeholders.
  • Manage sensitive and potentially contentious issues with professionalism and sound judgement.
  • Act as a senior representative in stakeholder meetings, community forums and public engagements.
  • Support issue resolution, complaints management and risk mitigation activities.
  • Develop innovative communication initiatives that foster transparency and trust.

Project Delivery & Reporting
  • Monitor stakeholder sentiment, emerging risks and community concerns.
  • Prepare executive-level reports, briefings and strategic insights.
  • Oversee engagement data collection, analysis and reporting.
  • Ensure engagement activities comply with legislative, regulatory and policy requirements.
  • Support procurement and administrative activities as required.

About You
To be successful, you will bring:
  • Extensive experience (10+ years) in community engagement, stakeholder relations, public affairs or communications leadership roles.
  • Demonstrated success delivering engagement strategies for major infrastructure, government or large-scale projects.
  • Experience managing complex stakeholder environments, including planning approvals, property acquisition, construction impacts and community issues.
  • Proven ability to lead high-performing teams and foster collaborative workplace cultures.
  • Strong strategic communications, negotiation and conflict resolution skills.
  • Experience preparing executive briefings, reports and strategic recommendations.
  • Strong project management capabilities with the ability to manage risks, priorities and competing stakeholder interests.

job.title: Safety Advisor
job.description:
Safety Advisor | Construction

$966 per day inclusive of super | Truganina
Initial 12-month contract | Long-term opportunity through to April 2028
Full-time | 3 days per week onsite

We are seeking an experienced Safety Advisor to provide dedicated health and safety assurance across a large-scale construction and operational environment in Truganina.

This role will work across a complex multi-contractor site, providing safety advice, assurance and oversight during construction activities that interface with operational teams. You’ll partner closely with internal safety and project stakeholders, the Principal Contractor, subcontractors and site leadership to support safe work practices and strong safety outcomes.

Importantly, this is an assurance and advisory role. It does not replace or assume the safety management responsibilities of the Principal Contractor or other employers undertaking work onsite.

The role
You will be responsible for:
  • Conducting site inspections, audits and spot checks across construction and operational activities
  • Monitoring high-risk construction activities and escalating safety concerns where required
  • Reviewing and verifying SWMS, permits and other relevant safety documentation
  • Providing advice on construction risk management and safe work practices
  • Supporting the implementation and adoption of OHS systems and processes
  • Identifying existing and emerging hazards and supporting corrective and preventative actions
  • Supporting incident investigations, inspections and reporting
  • Monitoring corrective actions and ensuring appropriate follow-through
  • Working closely with project, automation, safety, contractor and site leadership teams
  • Supporting safety initiatives and continual improvement activities
  • Coaching and influencing contractors, leaders and operational teams to strengthen safety behaviours
  • Supporting OHS compliance, reporting, data analysis and performance tracking
  • Preparing safety reports, metrics and KPIs for leadership and project stakeholders
  • Liaising with regulators and external stakeholders where required
  • Attending toolbox talks and site meetings as required
About youTo be successful, you will ideally bring:
  • Previous experience as an OHS / Safety Advisor within construction, major projects or another high-risk environment
  • Strong experience working across multi-contractor construction sites
  • A background in contractor safety management and safety assurance
  • Strong knowledge of Victorian OHS legislation, regulatory requirements and industry standards
  • Experience reviewing SWMS and other high-risk construction documentation
  • Experience supporting incident investigations and corrective actions
  • Confidence engaging with contractors, supervisors, site managers and senior stakeholders
  • Strong coaching, influencing and relationship-building skills
  • The ability to work independently, identify issues and proactively drive outcomes
  • Strong reporting, documentation and Microsoft Office skills

Qualifications
Ideally you will hold:
  • Certificate IV in Work Health and Safety or higher
  • ICAM investigation training or similar
  • Current Construction White Card
  • Current CPR and First Aid qualifications

The details
  • Rate: $966 per day inclusive of super
  • Location: Truganina, VIC
  • Contract: Initial 12 months, with the approved project duration currently extending to approximately April 2028
  • Hours: Full-time, with site operating hours generally between 6:00am and 4:00pm
  • Onsite requirement: Approximately 3 days per week onsite
  • Large-scale construction environment with significant contractor and operational interfaces

This is a strong opportunity for an experienced construction safety professional who enjoys being visible onsite, working collaboratively with multiple stakeholders and providing practical, credible safety assurance across a complex project environment.

job.title: Branch Manager
job.description:
Branch Manager | Canberra | FMCG & Distribution

Permanent | Full time

$165,000 – $175,000 + super | STI | Fully Maintained Company Vehicle
  • Senior leadership opportunity within a well-established national business
  • Lead a 50–60 person branch operation
  • Responsibility across sales, operations, transport, warehouse and customer service
  • Potential relocation assistance for the right candidate
The Opportunity

We are seeking an experienced Branch Manager to take overall responsibility for a large and established distribution operation in Canberra.

This is a senior leadership position with responsibility across sales, operations, transport, warehouse, administration and customer service, with a strong focus on branch profitability, customer service and team performance.

Reporting to senior management, you'll lead a team of approximately 50–60 employees and work closely with an experienced leadership group across the branch.

This is an opportunity for a confident and commercially minded leader to take ownership of an established operation, drive performance and identify opportunities to improve the way the business operates.

About the Role

You'll be responsible for:
  • Leading the day-to-day operations of the branch across sales, warehouse, transport and administration.
  • Delivering budgeted EBIT, revenue and profitability targets.
  • Managing branch budgets, forecasts, costs and financial performance.
  • Analysing P&L results and operational KPIs and taking corrective action where required.
  • Leading and developing a team of approximately 50–60 employees.
  • Driving customer growth, retention and service excellence.
  • Building strong relationships with customers, suppliers and internal stakeholders.
  • Managing inventory and ensuring customer demand is supported effectively.
  • Identifying new business opportunities and opportunities for growth.
  • Improving productivity, processes and operational efficiency.
  • Ensuring high standards of WHS, food safety, HACCP and Chain of Responsibility compliance.
  • Creating a culture of accountability, teamwork and continuous improvement.
  • Making timely decisions and providing clear direction across the branch.
About You

We're looking for an experienced operational leader who combines commercial understanding with strong people and operational leadership.

You'll ideally have:
  • Previous experience as a Branch Manager, Operations Manager, Distribution Manager, General Manager or similar.
  • Experience managing a sizeable workforce and multiple operational functions.
  • Strong commercial acumen and the ability to interpret P&L, budgets and financial performance.
  • Experience managing costs, productivity and operational KPIs.
  • Strong customer relationship and stakeholder management skills.
  • Excellent problem-solving and decision-making ability.
  • A visible, hands-on leadership style.
  • The confidence to challenge existing processes and drive positive change.
  • Strong communication and people management skills.
  • The ability to perform in a fast-paced, operational environment.
Experience in these areas will be highly regarded:
  • FMCG
  • Food distribution or foodservice
  • Grocery or wholesale distribution
  • Transport and logistics
  • Warehouse and distribution
  • High-volume operational environments
  • HACCP and food safety
  • Chain of Responsibility
  • WHS and psychosocial safety
Forklift or heavy vehicle licences are advantageous but not essential.

The Leadership Opportunity

This role will suit someone who enjoys being close to the operation and isn't afraid to make decisions.

You'll be taking over an established operation with experienced people and established ways of working.

The opportunity is to build on what's working, identify what can be improved and lead the team through positive change.

We're looking for someone who:
  • Takes ownership
  • Leads from the front
  • Makes decisions
  • Holds people accountable
  • Develops and supports their team
  • Builds strong customer relationships
  • Looks for better ways of doing things
  • Can balance people, customers and commercial outcomes
What's on Offer
  • $165,000 – $175,000 + super
  • Fully maintained company vehicle
  • STI / incentive program
  • Potential relocation assistance for the right candidate
  • Staff discounts and additional benefits
  • Opportunity to lead a substantial operation within an established national business
  • Genuine scope to influence operational performance and branch growth
Apply Now

If you're an experienced Branch or Operations Manager looking for a role where you can take genuine ownership and make a measurable impact, we'd like to hear from you.

Apply now with your updated resume and cover letter.

Early applications are encouraged, as shortlisting may commence before the closing date of Friday 2 October 2026.

Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. All applications will be treated confidentially.

As part of the recruitment process, successful candidates may be required to complete employment checks, which may include a medical assessment, drug and alcohol testing, National Police History Check and licence validation.

You can read more about our commitment to diversity and inclusion at https://www.chandlermacleod.com/diversity-and-inclusion.

job.title: Senior Project Manager (Civil Construction)
job.description:
Permanent | Cairns | Senior Project Leadership | Civil Construction


For an experienced civil Project Manager, this is an opportunity to take genuine ownership of project delivery, with responsibility extending well beyond programme management and reporting.

Based in Cairns, this permanent Senior Project Manager position sits within an established civil construction business delivering a diverse range of infrastructure projects.

This isn't a role sitting several layers removed from construction. You'll have overall responsibility for the project and its performance, leading the delivery team while maintaining oversight across commercial, programme, quality, safety, client and construction outcomes.

You'll be supported by an experienced engineering and quality team, including Project Engineers, Site Engineers and quality resources. The expectation is that you'll provide the leadership, direction and commercial oversight needed to keep projects performing from mobilisation through to completion.


What you'll be responsible for:


Your remit will cover the full lifecycle of civil construction projects, including:
  • Taking overall responsibility for project delivery from mobilisation through to completion
  • Leading Project Engineers, Site Engineers, supervisors, subcontractors and project support resources
  • Managing project budgets, forecasting, cost performance and overall commercial outcomes
  • Developing and driving construction programmes and ensuring key milestones are achieved
  • Managing procurement, subcontractors, variations and contractual requirements
  • Maintaining strong standards across safety, quality, compliance and project risk
  • Building effective relationships with clients, stakeholders and delivery partners
  • Providing practical leadership and direction to resolve issues and keep projects moving
  • Taking accountability for the performance of both the project and the team delivering it

Who we're looking for:


We're looking for someone who has built their career close to civil construction delivery and understands what it means to have genuine accountability for the whole project.

This will particularly suit someone experienced in a regional or mid-sized civil contractor environment, where Project Managers are expected to understand the commercial detail, know what's happening on site, lead their teams and take ownership of the final outcome.


To be considered, you'll need to bring:
  • A Degree in Civil Engineering (highly regarded)
  • Substantial experience in civil construction, with ideally five or more years operating at Project Manager level
  • A strong contractor-side background delivering civil infrastructure projects
  • Demonstrated experience taking projects from planning and mobilisation through construction to completion
  • Strong commercial capability across budgets, forecasting, procurement, contracts and cost control
  • Experience leading engineering, construction and subcontractor teams
  • A practical understanding of civil construction methodology, quality, safety and project risk
  • The judgement and leadership capability to make decisions, solve problems and remain accountable for project outcomes


Why consider the opportunity?


If you're looking for a role where you can have genuine influence over how projects are run, this is an opportunity to take ownership without being lost within a large corporate project structure.
You'll be close enough to the work to understand what's happening on site while having the autonomy and support to lead the broader project, team and commercial outcomes.


The opportunity offers:
  • A permanent Senior Project Manager position based in Cairns
  • Genuine end-to-end ownership of civil construction projects
  • Dedicated engineering and quality support
  • A hands-on leadership role with direct influence over project performance
  • An established civil construction environment where experienced Project Managers are trusted to lead
  • Exposure to a diverse range of civil infrastructure projects
This could particularly suit an experienced Senior Project Manager or Project Manager who has built a career within civil contracting and is ready for broader responsibility across projects, people and commercial performance.


If your experience aligns and you'd like a confidential discussion about the position, projects, package and opportunity to establish yourself in Cairns, apply now or contact Anna Dziopa at Chandler Macleod on 07 2140 6649.

job.title: Mechanical Maintainer
job.description:
Mechanical Maintainer
• Opportunity working at Rio Tinto
• Assignment via Chandler Macleod
• Safety-first culture with supportive teams

About the Opportunity
Rio Tinto is a global mining and materials company operating in 35 countries, producing the materials essential to modern life. Their operations are built on safety, innovation, inclusion and creating value for communities, customers and shareholders.

Through Rio Tinto’s partnership with Chandler Macleod, we are seeking an experienced Mechanical Maintainer to join our team at Dampier ports working a 5/5/4 roster with a mix of days and nights. The purpose of this role will be to provide a safe and efficient facility through the execution of mechanical fault finding, planned and opportune maintenance. This is a residential role only (Must live in Karratha or Dampier).
  
Reporting to the Maintenance Supervisor and working in a collaborative community, the role will require you to:
  • Complete preventative/corrective/planned /operational maintenance for all equipment in the fixed plant area, including but not limited to, conveyors, balanced machines, car dumpers
  • Conduct routine inspections of all fixed plant assets
  • Maintain a high level of safety awareness and comply with company policies and procedures
  • Actively contribute to continuous improvement projects by increasing safety whilst reducing risk and cost
  • Utilise SAP to ensure that maintenance tasks are recorded, assigned correctly and completed to the relevant standard / specification
  • Isolate equipment for maintenance and operational tasks
  • Work safely within Rio Tinto procedures
About you
  • A Mechanical Engineering/Fitting/Fabrication Trade Qualification
  • Experience working on the following equipment: car dumpers, stackers, reclaimers and ship loaders
  • Proficiency in motor/gearbox, Pulley and Bucketwheel changeouts, Laser Alignment, Dogging experience and Rigging experience as well as ability to conduct high quality maintenance inspections.
  • Able to work a varied swing with a mix of days and nights
  • Previous mining or heavy industry experience
  • Commitment to work the rostered shifts
  • Strong teamwork and communication skills
  • Dedication to everyone’s safety
  • Current C Class manual drivers’ license (HR desirable) 
  • Relevant trade qualifications and certificates (Working at Heights and confined spaces)
  • Ability to pass pre-employment medical and other testing
If you are safety-driven professional with experience in maintenance operations, we want to hear from you. Apply now and become a key contributor to safe, compliant and successful port operations in Dampier.

Why Join Chandler Macleod?
Chandler Macleod is one of Australia’s most experienced workforce partners. You’ll receive a competitive pay rate paid weekly, superannuation on all hours worked, access to our Employee Assistance Program, a dedicated Chandler-Rio Tinto support team, simple digital onboarding, and access to future Rio Tinto assignments.

Apply Now!
Ready to take the next step? Apply today to join Chandler Macleod for an exciting onsite assignment with Rio Tinto. Applications close 30/10/2026. Chandler Macleod reserves the right to close applications earlier if suitable candidates are identified.

job.title: Capability Development Support
job.description:
Chandler Macleod is recruiting on behalf of our client for an experienced Capability Development Support Officer to support a high-profile Defence capability development program. This opportunity is ideal for professionals with strong governance, administration, project coordination, records management, and stakeholder engagement experience within complex environments.

The Opportunity
We are seeking a Capability Development Support Officer to provide governance, coordination, information management and administrative support across a major Defence capability development program.
Working closely with program stakeholders, you will play a key role in supporting governance forums, coordinating taskings, maintaining records and documentation, and ensuring effective information management across multiple concurrent activities.
This role will suit a highly organised professional who can manage competing priorities while maintaining strong stakeholder relationships and attention to detail.

Key Responsibilities:
  • Coordinate correspondence, information flows and shared document repositories.
  • Support governance boards, committees, working groups and stakeholder meetings.
  • Prepare agendas, briefing packs, decision-support documentation and meeting minutes.
  • Manage action registers, task tracking and reporting requirements.
  • Coordinate stakeholder taskings and consolidate responses for governance artefacts.
  • Maintain records and document repositories in accordance with information management requirements.
  • Support audit, assurance and compliance activities.
  • Assist with workforce coordination, business management and administrative functions.
  • Provide broader program coordination support as required.

Essential Skills & Experience
  • Strong experience in project support, governance, administration or program coordination roles.
  • Excellent Microsoft Office and collaboration tool skills.
  • Strong organisational and information management capabilities.
  • Highly developed written and verbal communication skills.
  • Demonstrated ability to coordinate multiple stakeholders and competing priorities.
  • Experience supporting governance forums, boards, committees or project teams.
  • Experience managing records, correspondence and document control processes.

Desirable Experience
  • Previous experience within Defence or Government environments.
  • Exposure to capability development, ICT programs, acquisition or program delivery activities.
  • Knowledge of governance frameworks and information management processes.
  • Experience using records management and collaboration systems.
  • Understanding of capability development or program governance environments.

Contract Details
Contract Term: 1 January 2027 – 31 December 2027
Extension Options: Up to 2 x 12-month extensions available
Location: Russell, ACT
Hours: 40 hours per week
Security Clearance: NV1 (Mandatory)
